386YE Autumn Equinox Conclave sessions.d: The Conclave renewed amity with Sadogua, Zakalwe and Barien, but an enmity declaration against the Asavean 'Cowled One' failed. It called on the Senate to build a fane of Sung in Apulian and advised avoiding rituals involving Meraud's feral lions. The orders were sent to Faraden, Axos, the flooded Brass Coast and the spreading marshes of Madruga. Serenius Starsong, Alexander Tallstag and Gaius Starfall i Riqueza took titles. Mana reservoirs and Umbar's Exquisite Visage were interdicted. Two dossiers were bought from the City of Locks for 130 tempest jade. The Gift of the Wily Broker was traded to the Black Sand Circle for Eye of Ruby and Sapphire, and Stag Knight's Glory went to the Thule Ambassador.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Day's statement to Zakalwe said every pearl issued by the Polemarch of Highwatch is accounted for and ready for use on the Druj front.
n.Grendel: The Black Sand Circle in Grendel-held Beoraidh received a copy of The Gift of the Wily Broker in exchange for Eye of Ruby and Sapphire, which the Golden Pyramid grandmaster will receive at the Winter Solstice.
n.Navarr: The Archmage of Night confirmed amity with Sadogua and thanked the eternal for continuing to protect the college of the Lyceum and for boons given to Navarr magicians, with interest expressed in more permanent wards.
n.Thule: The Conclave disseminated the Stag Knight's Glory ritual to the Thule Ambassador to the Empire, funded by Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided.

t.Mareave: A copy of The Gift of the Wily Broker was created and disseminated to the Black Sand Circle in Mareave as part of a ritual-text exchange agreed with the Golden Pyramid.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The Black Sand Circle in Beoraidh received The Gift of the Wily Broker and is to provide Eye of Ruby and Sapphire to the Golden Pyramid grandmaster at the Winter Solstice.

386YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Astolat, Casinea, Hahnmark, Kahraman, Karov, Morrow, Semmerholm, Tassato, Upwold and Volodmartz. The Senate appointed generals for nine armies, with two for the Quiet Step, along with many stewards, custodians and other office holders. The Synod chose Sabella of the Silent Tide as Cardinal of Loyalty with 264 votes and Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra as Cardinal of Pride. The Military Council appointed Natalia 'The Falcon' Barossa as Quartermaster General and strategoi for Highguard, Varushka and Wintermark. Bourse auctions and votes allocated mines, wayleaves and other seats. Tallis Hart received 934 votes as Castellan of Spiral Castle, and Torven Krigerson paid 420 thrones for the Great Pits of Ennerlund.

n.Dawn: Dawn returned two senators: Cerys de Rosier for Astolat and Amicia of the Semmerlak for Semmerholm.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: no Grendel senator or national title appears in these results, and no senator is listed for Mareave.
n.Highguard: Highguard returned Solomon as senator for Casinea, and the Military Council appointed Balaam as Strategos of Highguard.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast returned Ramos I Inigo I Raqueza as senator for Kahraman.
n.The League: The League returned Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato as senator for Tassato.
n.The Marches: The Marches returned Johnny Tailor as senator for Upwold.
n.Urizen: Urizen returned Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard as senator for Morrow.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned Myshki Marishka Letuchaya for Karov and Ostrik Vulpe for Volodmartz, and the Military Council appointed Doubravka Nadjaovna Vanek-Vessely as Strategos of Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark returned Ruana Markling as senator for Hahnmark, and the Military Council appointed Aeolwulf as Strategos of Wintermark.

t.Astolat: Cerys de Rosier was elected senator for Astolat.
t.Casinea: Solomon was elected senator for Casinea.
t.Hahnmark: Ruana Markling was elected senator for Hahnmark.
t.Kahraman: Ramos I Inigo I Raqueza was elected senator for Kahraman.
t.Karov: Myshki Marishka Letuchaya was elected senator for Karov.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: no senator for Mareave is listed among this summit's election results.
t.Morrow: Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard was elected senator for Morrow.
t.Semmerholm: Amicia of the Semmerlak was elected senator for Semmerholm.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was elected senator for Tassato. Magnus Carolus Sanguino Rezia di Tassato was appointed Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Upwold: Johnny Tailor was elected senator for Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: Ostrik Vulpe was elected senator for Volodmartz.

386YE Autumn Equinox Military Council or.d: The Jotun had seized Southmoor, Greensward, Ore Hills and Chalkdowns and reinstated Jarl Haakon. The Marcher Tusks and Highguard's Granite Pillar stood in defence while Highborn, Marcher, Orc, Dawnish, League and Wintermark armies attacked. The Towerjacks, Citadel Guard and Northern Eagle hurried to Redoubt amid rumours of a Children of Wrecks attack. Imperial forces withdrew from the Brass Coast and Ayereed, leaving the Winter Sun alone in Mareave. In Therunin, Navarr, Varushkan and Dawnish armies struck at the Druj after a costly battle to save Feverwater Steading. General Archavion Wolfborne ordered the Gryphon's Pride to seize the Fangs mine from the Rahvin. Only the Wolves of War, Black Thorns and Iron Helms earned the guerdon.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky joined the Mournwold offensive and the Golden Sun kept up its grinding advance in Therunin. General Archavion Wolfborne set the Gryphon's Pride to seize the Fangs from the Rahvin, an act that will bring the full force of the law on him and his captains.
n.Druj: Having failed to destroy Feverwater Steading or rouse the Sweetglades vallorn, the Druj in Therunin faced attacks from four Imperial armies. The Gryphon's Pride's strike on the Rahvin was feared to wreck any hope of peace with other Druj slaves.
n.Grendel: The Empire's probing strike into Ayereed fell back, leaving only the Winter Sun in Mareave. A great Grendel force remained camped on the Madruga coast and Commander Gallum Fiersach still held Mora's Rock in Feroz.
n.Highguard: All three Highborn armies marched on the Mournwold in a crusade invoking Synod judgement 117. The Granite Pillar held a strategic defence while the Seventh Wave force-marched from Ayereed and the Valiant Pegasus advanced on Southmoor.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Autumn Hammers and Summer Storm made a steady conquest against the Jotun in the Mournwold. The Winter Sun fell back to give ground in Mareave and was its only defender against the Grendel.
n.Jotun: Tens of thousands of Jotun held four Mournwold regions under Jarl Haakon and now faced a dozen Imperial armies. It was uncertain whether they would stand, sweep into Bregasland or strike toward Tassato.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns made a balanced attack in Therunin and earned the guerdon, while Isaella's Dance struck through the Barrens into Eastring with poison thorns. The Quiet Step, under Vesna Borkovna Prochnost, mounted a solid defence of Miaren.
n.The Brass Coast: With Feroz freed, the Burning Falcon and Fire of the South left for a desperate reinforcement of Astolat and the Red Wind Corsairs rested in Tassato. That left no Imperial armies on the uncertain Brass Coast.
n.The League: The Towerjacks dug in at Redoubt, their orders mourning the fall of General Barossa. The Wolves of War made a balanced attack on the Mournwold and earned the guerdon.
n.The Marches: The Tusks stood in strategic defence of the Mournwold while the Bounders and Drakes attacked the Jotun. The Strong Reeds lay low in Bregasland and were the only army standing there against the Jotun.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard marched from Morrow to a solid defence of Redoubt, reinforced by League and Varushkan armies against a rumoured Wrecker attack. Meanwhile the Golden Axe came to Zenith.
n.Varushka: In his last orders, General Belakov sent the Golden Axe to give ground in Zenith. The Iron Helms, quickened with cold-meat magic, attacked the Druj in Therunin for the guerdon, and the Northern Eagle harried foes in Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: The Narwhal's Spear sought the foe in the Mournwold while the Green Shield billeted in Upwold. The Bloodcloaks tended the fallen and the Fist of the Mountains read the signs, both in Tassato.

t.Astolat: The Burning Falcon and Fire of the South marched here in desperate reinforcement, while Isaella's Dance left Astolat for Therunin.
t.Ayereed: The Empire's probing strike fell back from Ayereed, with the Seventh Wave, Winter Sun and Golden Axe all departing.
t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds lay low here as the only army facing the Jotun, whose enchanted castle rose over Gravenrock, and a Jotun sweep into the territory was feared.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched from Casinea to the Mournwold.
t.Feroz: Feroz was declared freed and the Imperial armies there departed, but Commander Gallum Fiersach still held the fort of Mora's Rock.
t.Madruga: With Imperial forces withdrawn, Madruga remained split between factions, and a great Grendel force was camped on the fens that were once the Siroc Plains.
t.Mareave: The Winter Sun gave ground in Mareave as its sole defender, wary of Grendel armies following from Ayereed.
t.Miaren: The Quiet Step returned from the Mournwold to mount a solid defence of Miaren.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes, who had smashed ships on the river Meade, marched from Mitwold, and the Autumn Hammers passed through it to the Mournwold.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard marched from Morrow to defend Redoubt.
t.Mournwold: With the Jotun holding four regions, a dozen Imperial armies converged on the Mournwold, the Tusks and Granite Pillar defending while the rest attacked.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe's general listed Ossium among the territories his army had fought in.
t.Redoubt: Storm-wracked Redoubt was reinforced by the Towerjacks, Citadel Guard and Northern Eagle amid rumours of a Children of Wrecks attack.
t.Tassato: The Red Wind Corsairs, Bloodcloaks and Fist of the Mountains recuperated in Tassato, which was thought vulnerable to a Jotun strike.
t.The Barrens: The Gryphon's Pride was ordered to seize the Fangs mine from the Rahvin, whom the Senate had declared protected foreigners, and Isaella's Dance passed through on its way to Therunin.
t.Therunin: After a costly battle to save Feverwater Steading, the Golden Sun, Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance and Iron Helms struck at the Druj amid spreading vallorn corruption.
t.Upwold: The Green Shield billeted in Upwold while the Summer Storm left for the Mournwold.
t.Zenith: The Golden Axe moved to Zenith to give ground, rest and celebrate under its departing general.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Chalkdowns was among the regions seized by the Jotun, where the Imperial counter-offensive was now directed.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Greensward lay under Jotun control after their seizure of the Mourn, facing the Imperial armies massing against them.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Though held by the Jotun, the Ore Hills saw a victory by Imperial heroes that inspired the people of the Mourn to rise.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Jotun-held Southmoor was the target of the Seventh Wave, Valiant Pegasus and Bounders as they sought to liberate it.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Isaella's Dance was ordered to strike into Eastring through the Barrens with poison thorns against the Druj.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Imperial heroes prevented the Druj from rousing the Sweetglades vallorn, though Spring corruption still crept across the territory.

386YE Autumn Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 751 thrones and two crowns. Feroz was assigned to the Brass Coast. The Watcher of the Semmerlak was created and elected, and the Overseer of the Gloaming Road and the Keeper of the Crystal Vale were abrogated. Proposals to amend the Crystal Architect and the Keeper of the Cox failed, and the Stipulator of Stipends was struck down as unconstitutional. Funds went to the Diplomatenschloss (125 thrones), the Five Cities Military Academy (100) and Temeschwar's great works (200). New works included the Library of Worth, Last Battle Wayhouse, Landskeeper's Study, Curstag's Way and several sinecures. The Reinos spy network was decommissioned and Empress Vesna drew 250 thrones for the Dawnish army.

n.Dawn: The Challenger in Waiting will continue to be appointed by the Dawnish Assembly, with new duties to measure the Throne's Virtue, and Empress Vesna drew 250 thrones through the Hand of the Chancellor for the continued construction of a Dawnish army.
n.Druj: The Last Battle Wayhouse was commissioned in the Bleaks as a strategic tool against the Druj, providing reconnaissance into Sarangrave, while an appraisal on damaging Mallum army supply was withdrawn.
n.Grendel: The Senate assigned Grendel-held Feroz to the Brass Coast and commissioned an appraisal of how to disrupt relations between each Salt Lord and their allies, while an Ambassador to the Grendel will be appointed at the Winter Solstice.
n.Highguard: A monument celebrating the work to end discrimination against the lineaged in Highguard and the wider Empire was built in Bastion, while the proposed conversion of Reikos's Keeper of the Cox into the Keeper of the Watch failed.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were given the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons, to be first elected at the Winter Solstice, and funded the Library of Worth folly in Skarsind to preserve a word and symbol each season.
n.Jotun: The Imperial Spymaster announced that the Empire's spy network in Jotun-held Reinos would be decommissioned over the coming season, citing leaked secrets.
n.Navarr: The Generals of Navarr will appoint the keeper of the new Last Battle Wayhouse, two artefacts became regalia for the Quiet Step and Black Thorns generals, the Black Thorns received the Guerdon, and Thornsong House began research into a tonic against vallorn miasma.
n.The League: League cities gained substantial investment: 100 thrones for the Five Cities Military Academy, 200 for Temeschwar's great works, Curstag's Way in Spiral, the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy in Sarvos and continued work on the Garden City of Holberg.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained the Landskeeper's Study in Upwold, the Hartford Brewery in Stockmarch and a Bounders Hall in Meade, with an appraisal passed to expand the Upwold Seed Exchange.
n.Urizen: The Temple of the Four Winds was converted to a monastery, the Cascade of Living Flame was built in Morrow, and the bid to make the Crystal Architect an Imperial title failed, while the Golden Cascade proposal was withdrawn.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly will now appoint the Grieftender of the Forgotten, the Bone Hives were expanded and volhovs will make bequests to the new Watcher of the Semmerlak, though the Gallery of Memories failed.
n.Wintermark: The Strategos of Wintermark now holds the Vale's Might mana sinecure for ten crystals a season, and new sinecures were built at Floerstrand in Sermersuaq and the Proud Quill Parcel in Hahnmark.

t.Bastion: A monument to those who worked against discrimination of the lineaged was constructed in Sybella, Sybella's Cross, to Lady Josephine's design.
t.Feroz: The Senate assigned the territory of Feroz, then held by the Grendel, to the Brass Coast.
t.Hahnmark: The Vale's Might sinecure in Wood Heath passed to the Strategos of Wintermark, and the Proud Quill Parcel herb sinecure was built in Kalpaheim.
t.Mitwold: A Bounders Hall was built in Meade, funded by the houses of Talbot and Mudd, creating the Bailiff of Meade and a place for Marcher beaters to send their units.
t.Morrow: The Cascade of Living Flame, a self-funded mana sinecure appointed by Urizen senators, was built in Peregro.
t.Reikos: A proposal to turn the Keeper of the Cox into the Keeper of the Watch, guarding the Grove of Golden Cox, failed.
t.Reinos: The Imperial Spymaster announced that the spy network in Reinos would be dismantled over the coming season.
t.Spiral: Curstag's Way, a Grand Highway linking Redoubt, Spiral and Mareave, was constructed as a great work in Spiral.
t.The Barrens: The Last Battle Wayhouse was built in the Bleaks, and a statue of the White Bear was raised in the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn in Dawnguard.
t.Upwold: The Landskeeper's Study was built in Ashbrook and the Hartford Brewery in Stockmarch, while an appraisal was passed to expand the Upwold Seed Exchange.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: The Keeper of the Crystal Vale was abrogated and the Vale's Might mana sinecure here now supports the Strategos of Wintermark.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Cascade of Living Flame, a ten-wain mithril mana sinecure, was constructed in Peregro.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The Landskeeper's Study mana ministry was built in Oakwood, its Keeper appointed annually by Marcher senators to spread knowledge of farm enchantment.

386YE Autumn Equinox Synod judgements.d: The General Assembly upheld Sabella of the Silent Tide's veto (2880-140), so the ban on preaching in Asavea did not become law. Many assemblies pledged support and funds for the Asavean effort. Highguard, the League and Varushka issued mandates committing themselves to Navarr's war on the vallorn. Several nations sent patrols against Druj beachheads. Cardinals who accepted Axou hallowings of false virtues were condemned or called to inquisition. The Ore Hills rebels and Ravadi Founder's Dance were recognised as exemplars. Marcher and Freeborn farmers were sent to help Mareave. Twenty-four appointments were made. Rewardings exhausted the Virtue Fund, leaving several upheld rewards unpaid.

n.Dawn: Dawn's mandate set the Vigilant to patrol the Barrens against the Druj. Its assembly urged troubadours to preach to the Barrens' inhabitants or drive them out, and called on the Dawnish to settle the empty lands. The Highborn invited Dawnish troubadours to teach at Bastion, and the assembly pledged to join Navarr against the vallorn.
n.Druj: Urizen, Dawn, Navarr and Varushka sent patrols that make Druj beachheads in Morrow, Zenith, the Barrens, Therunin and Ossium harder to claim. Navarr's assembly pledged to keep fighting them in Therunin, while the General Assembly told priests to challenge cries of "Death to the Druj".
n.Grendel: Urizen's assembly warned Redoubt to prepare for attack by the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks. The Vigilance assembly urged pilgrims in Mareave to root out those working in Grendel interests. A penance condemned Raine Tealeaf for once conspiring to aid the Grendel against Spiral.
n.Highguard: A Highborn greater-majority mandate committed Highguard to fighting the vallorn: the grey pilgrims stop walking the trods, and the nation can support four armies instead of three. The assembly also offered peerless kinship to help Navarr raise an army, called for the Thundering Tide to be reborn, and summoned several Highborn to inquisition for ignoring field commanders' orders.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly invited Urizen into Mareave to recover lost histories. Its mandate sent the Illarawm to open peaceful talks with the Brine Turtle elders. Marcher and Freeborn farmers were dispatched to help make the territory's land flourish.
n.Jotun: Navarr's assembly rejected two statements refusing to change how they fight the Jotun, but upheld the Black Scar's pride in their deeds. Marcher and Varushkan judgements urged resistance to the Jotun conquest of the Mournwold and the defence of Bregasland.
n.Navarr: Navarr's war on the vallorn drew support from Highguard, the League, Varushka, Dawn and Urizen, and Navarr resolved to stand together on that long road. Its mandate will defend Therunin's borders once the territory is reclaimed. Its assembly embraced the Great Forest Orcs and backed the Throne taking control of the Quiet Step.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn praised their corsairs smuggling preachers into Asavea and asked for safe passage home for the Asavean priests of the Temple of the Black Bull. They warned Quzar to avoid Tharim's heralds and urged that swamped Madruga be mapped first. A mandate sending Freeborn farmers to Mareave costs every Brass Coast congregation a rank of production.
n.The League: The League's mandate committed it to aiding Navarr against the vallorn, and the Highborn invited League bishops to teach at Bastion. The assembly celebrated 250 years of Holberg in the Empire, backed a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg, and invited the Sand Fishers to Anvil. It also castigated Senator Gulia of Sarvos for voting to ban preaching in Asavea.
n.The Marches: Marcher priests urged Bregasland to fortify and offered Alderly's hospitality to soldiers resisting the Jotun. They warned of Agramant's servants in Upwold and Mitwold and revoked Hal Talbot as Senator for Mitwold. Their mandate sent farmers to Mareave at the cost of congregation production at home.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named on the page; it is linked only through its hold on part of Ossium, whose borders Varushkan patrols now guard.
n.Urizen: Urizen's mandate set patrols on the borders of Morrow and Zenith against the Druj, reducing taxation by ten thrones. The assembly warned Redoubt of a Grendel threat, accepted the Imperial Orcs' invitation to recover Urizeni histories in Mareave, and pledged magical support for a Navarr army.
n.Varushka: Varushkan mandates committed the nation to aiding Navarr against the vallorn, turned the Iron Helms away from cruelty towards dark magics and curses, and set patrols on Ossium's borders. The assembly also called the Ketsov family to inquisition and urged the faithful not to mourn the mythical Vardas.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark assembly refused to back Navarr to the exclusion of all else, and instead urged its people to provision their halls for hard winters ahead. Jorma Steelhail and Empress Britta were added to the Chronicle of Heroism, and the Suaq pledged to seek weregild for any harm done to the hylje.

t.Bastion: League bishops and Dawnish troubadours were invited to teach at the Holy City in Bastion on its completion. A Marcher mandate urging support for it was not enacted because of the Vardas revelations.
t.Bregasland: The Marcher assembly urged Bregasland's citizens to fortify against the enemy by breaking ditches, flooding fields, blocking roads and spreading the swamp.
t.Feroz: The Freeborn assembly asked their generals to grant the Asavean priests of the Temple of the Black Bull in Feroz safe passage home.
t.Holberg: The League celebrated 250 years of Holberg in the Empire and appointed a new Mistress of Ceremonies. It backed a Faraden trading enclave in the city and invited the Sand Fishers of north-western Holberg to Anvil.
t.Kahraman: The Freeborn welcomed Imperial and Faraden pilgrims to the Azure Chorus and asked the Azure Sutannir to protect travellers there.
t.Madruga: The Freeborn assembly warned the people of Quzar to avoid Tharim's heralds. It also urged that the swamp now covering much of southern Madruga be mapped before anyone tries to reclaim it.
t.Mareave: Marcher and Freeborn farmers were sent to help the territory's agriculture, and Imperial Orc Illarawm were sent to open talks with the Brine Turtles. Urizen was invited to recover Urizeni histories, and the Vigilant were urged to root out Grendel agents.
t.Mitwold: The Marcher assembly warned of Agramant's servants and the Stone Circle in Mitwold, and revoked Hal Talbot as its senator. Its congregations suffer a rank penalty as farmers leave for Mareave.
t.Morrow: An Urizen mandate set the Vigilant to patrol Morrow's borders, making a Druj beachhead harder to claim.
t.Mournwold: Judgements lamented the Jotun conquest of the Mournwold. The leaders of the 326YE Ore Hills rebellion were recognised as exemplars of Pride, and Alderly offered shelter to soldiers resisting the Jotun.
t.Ossium: A Varushkan mandate set patrols on Ossium's borders, other than the Webwood, against the Druj. The Ketsov family were called to inquisition over their conduct in the territory.
t.Redoubt: Urizen's assembly told the people of Redoubt to watch the coast for the Children of Wrecks and the Grendel and to guard the Ribbon of Salt and Evenstar. Adelmar's Shrine there was offered as a teaching place for every weapon style.
t.Reikos: The Highborn resolved to watch for the right moment to repair the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters, which was destroyed by scions of Cold Sun.
t.Spiral: The Silent Bell was directed to investigate the Hand of Dumon around the Black Plateau. Raine Tealeaf was given penance for plotting to let Spiral fall to the Grendel, and the League's Reckoning negotiation with Urizen over Spiral was put to inquisition.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: donations to the Virtue Fund were received at Tassato's counting house.
t.The Barrens: Dawn's mandate put patrols on the Barrens' borders against the Druj. The Dawnish assembly called for preaching to its inhabitants, or driving them out, and for settling its empty lands, while a penance criticised the Throne's veto of the Rahvin treaty.
t.Therunin: With Therunin under Druj conquest, Highguard offered peerless kinship to help Navarr raise an army there and was asked to guide its restless souls. A Navarr mandate will patrol its borders once it is reclaimed.
t.Upwold: The Marcher assembly raised the hue and cry against Agramant's servants and the Stone Circle in Upwold. Its congregations suffer a rank penalty as farmers leave for Mareave.
t.Zenith: An Urizen mandate set the Vigilant to patrol Zenith's borders, making a Druj beachhead harder to claim.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers were praised as guardians of the Flaxen Pillars of Misericorde, for repaying their sawmill loan and for making a home there. The Prince of the Misericorde Market joined the invitation for them to come to Anvil.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: the Rebeshof Roadwarden was among those inviting the Sand Fishers to Anvil.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: A rewarding to fund a shrine of the Way in Beoraidh, aimed at bringing that small foreign nation to the faith, was not upheld.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Mentioned in passing: the region is not discussed; Icarion appears only in the name of the priest Vigilance Athan Icarion.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: House Leveret and Alderly, never held as thralls under the Jotun, offered a bed and a bowl to any Imperial soldier resisting the Jotun.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The leaders of the 326YE Ore Hills rebellion were recognised as exemplars of Pride, and Varushka celebrated the miners' courage against the Jotun.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Webwood was excluded from Varushka's border patrols. The Ketsov family were called to inquisition over their actions towards the Trudniki of the Webwood.

386YE Autumn Equinox event schedule.d: Eight nations held senatorial elections in their camps on Saturday afternoon, each by its own method. Examples include the Brass Coast auction, the Highguard inquisition of candidates, the Urizen demos and the Wintermark jars. Tally of the Votes elections for national titles ran from 3:30pm to 5:30pm across eight nations. The Marches' Singing Caves Bourse seat had been taken by barbarians, so its winner would serve one season and receive only the production already retrieved. Other scheduled events included battles off Anvil on Saturday and Sunday, several Senate sessions, the Imperial Bourse auction, Grandmaster elections, the Inquisition of Brother Luke and the Balancing of Ephisis' Scale.

n.Dawn: Dawn elected senators for Semmerholm and Astolat at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney. It also held a Tally of the Votes at Glory Square for the Castellan of Spiral Castle and the Reeve of Boar's Market.
n.Highguard: Highguard began its inquisition of candidates for the Casinea senatorship at 2:00pm.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held a Tally of the Votes at the Fire Pit at 5:30pm to elect the Legion Engineer and the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
n.Navarr: Navarr held a Tally of the Votes at the Standing Circle at 5:30pm to elect the Thornsinger. A Thorns Collective meeting was also scheduled in the Military Council tent.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast began its auction for the Kahraman senatorship at 2:00pm. At the Waypoint it held a Tally of the Votes for the Red Depths, the Mistress of the Dust Parador and the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills.
n.The League: The League elected the senator for Tassato, with the presentation of collected bonds at 3:30pm.
n.The Marches: Marcher landowners gathered at 1:30pm to elect Upwold's senator. A Tally at the Community Hall elected the Singing Caves, the Alder of Meade and the Master of the Root and Stem; the Singing Caves seat had fallen to barbarians, so it carried only one season's retrieved production.
n.Urizen: Urizen's demos for the Morrow senatorship ran from 1:00pm to 1:45pm, and the Brilliant Star was elected by Tally near the Net of Heaven. An Urizen Magician's Meeting was also held on Friday.
n.Varushka: Varushka began questioning candidates for the Volodmartz and Karov senatorships at 1:45pm. At the Central Hearth it elected the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Bargainer of the Iron Tower and the Tolvoli Butcher by Tally.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark placed jars down for 30 minutes from 2:00pm to elect Hahnmark's senator. At the Tree of Names it elected the Pride of Ikka's Tears and the Keeper of the Runegrott.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator was elected by Dawn at 2:30pm, ahead of the next regular election for the seat at the Winter Solstice 386YE.
t.Casinea: Casinea's senator was chosen through a Highguard inquisition of candidates beginning at 2:00pm.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator was elected by Wintermark's jar vote, with jars placed down for 30 minutes from 2:00pm.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman's senatorship was decided by Brass Coast auction beginning at 2:00pm.
t.Karov: Karov's senator was elected through Varushkan questioning of candidates from 1:45pm, ahead of the next regular election for the title at the Summer Solstice 387YE.
t.Morrow: Morrow's senator was chosen by an Urizen demos held between 1:00pm and 1:45pm.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's senator was elected by Dawn at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting was among the titles elected in the Imperial Orc Tally of the Votes.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle was among the titles elected in the Dawnish Tally of the Votes.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator was elected by the League, with the presentation of collected bonds at 3:30pm.
t.Upwold: Upwold's senator was elected when Marcher landowners gathered at 1:30pm.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's senator was elected through Varushkan questioning of candidates beginning at 1:45pm.

386YE Autumn Equinox interlude.d: Mandates opened opportunities to hunt Agramant followers. League units could do so in Holberg under Kanute Adelaar van Holberg, and units across the Empire under Jared of the Sentinels Tower, though that search cost every business and farm 18 rings. Fleets could race under Rhianos's challenge, smuggle Way missionaries into Asavea, or harass the Asavean blockade of Sumaah. The Guerdon, set at 250 thrones, went only to units supporting the Wolves of War. Urizen citizens went to help the Marcher harvest while Marcher priests travelled to Urizen. The Serpent's Curse weakened Urizen congregations, Sermersuaq prospered, and Dho'uala continued to hinder Dawnish and Varushkan fleets.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets continued to suffer a one rank production penalty while the sovereign Dho'uala haunted the Semmerlak.
n.The League: League military units could join Kanute Adelaar van Holberg's hunt for the Agramant cannibal conspiracy in Holberg. Holberg's fleets are now free of Dho'uala's penalty following Ivana Petara Vodjavic's mandate.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens left their work to help the Marcher harvest, halving the Doyen of the Spires' codification speed. Visiting Marcher priests boosted Urizen congregations, but the Serpent's Curse cost them two votes and one liao each, and Urizen fleets were barred from thwarting the blockade.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets continued to suffer Dho'uala's one rank production penalty and were excluded from the effort to disrupt the Asavean blockade of Sumaah.
n.Wintermark: The people of Sermersuaq came together against the harsh winter and Agramant's schemes, so every personal resource there gains 22 extra rings until the Winter Solstice.

t.Holberg: League units could hunt the Agramant cannibal conspiracy in Holberg, with a chance to bring it down at the Autumn Equinox if enough strength is committed. Holberg's fleets no longer suffer Dho'uala's penalty.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's people united in defiance of winter and Agramant, granting every personal resource there an extra 22 rings until the Winter Solstice 386YE.
t.The Semmerlak: The sovereign Dho'uala continued to haunt the Semmerlak with eerie lights and disappearances. The Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak still cannot buy ilium and pays more for weirwood.

386YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: Rane Shard-Bearer delivered the Throne's address. Navarr mobilised against the vallorn, with League and Varushkan mandates in support. The Lepidean Library's claim that Vardas never existed provoked a crisis of faith that also stalls the Sandling academy. Naomi of Virtue's Rest reported on a possible Jotun ceasefire, and Eilian Sweetwater appraised Mareave. The Scorrero flooded from Kahraman to Madruga, and a Deadwood Knight threatened Dawn from Weirwater and Karov. The Marcher smiths were reconciled with their nation. Conjunction results included Governor Rahab's assassination, a Jotun Burhfæst established in Gravenmarch, and heavy Imperial losses at Peregro. Oran, Nemoria, Kavor and Vezak stayed closed to Imperial fleets.

n.Dawn: Dawn was offered a Grand Tour tourney and a proposed national fayre at Anvil, while the Deadwood Knight prepared to attack and the fate of the Barrens remained unresolved between the Assembly and the senators.
n.Druj: Synod judgements urged citizens bordering the Druj to act against them. Druj forces were slowed in Lower Tarn Valley and defeated in the Bleaks and Grimfen Mire, but they inflicted heavy Imperial casualties at Peregro.
n.Grendel: Governor Rahab was assassinated in Madruga and Grendel forces were beaten in Siluri and Ayereed. Citizens began cataloguing the weaknesses of Grendel monsters, and the port of Oran stayed closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn wayfarers were among those urged to preach in Asavea, and citizens of Casinea were tagged in a winds of magic entry.
n.Imperial Orcs: An appraisal found costly ways to deal with the recalcitrant orcs of southern Mareave, and further investment opportunities emerged there, including from the Tamazi sept.
n.Jotun: Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out what might make a ceasefire with the Jotun more likely. The Jotun established a Burhfæst in Gravenmarch but were defeated in Iron Stand, Meade March and the Suaq Wastes, where Urse Longarm was among the slain.
n.Navarr: Navarr committed to the final battle against the vallorn, recalled its stridings and mobilised for war, with opportunities to raise three new armies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Scorrero rose from Kahraman through Segura to Madruga, washing away the Blight and the Dry Patricians with destructive and transformative force, while several Madrugan conjunctions defeated the nation's foes.
n.The League: The League Assembly gained three mandates on how to support Navarr against the vallorn. Sarvos debated the Sarcophan enclave and Vandersaar investment, and Temeschwar's rat plague was controlled but not ended.
n.The Marches: Marcher friars shared their understanding of virtue in Urizen while Urizeni helped bring in the Marcher harvest, and the lost smiths of Oakwood were reconciled with the nation.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the civil service summarised a report from Otkodov, and Thule watchers were tagged in a winds of magic entry.
n.Urizen: Urizeni helped bring in the Marcher harvest in exchange for Marcher friars preaching in the spires, and Urizen's citizens were stirred by calls to act against the Druj.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Assembly gained three mandates on supporting Navarr against the vallorn, and the Deadwood Knight, a lieutenant of the Howling Queen, gathered strength in southern Karov.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesa's senator Rane Shard-Bearer gave the Throne's address. Ishal mystics sought new ways to protect Kallavesa, and the Rising Tide presented proposals for Wintermark.

t.Ayereed: The General of the Red Wind Corsairs defeated Grendel and Asavean forces at Dunreagh's Brush and delivered 12 wains of mithril.
t.Bay of Catazar: Citizens around the Bay of Catazar began gathering veterans' knowledge of the Grendel and Children of Wrecks monsters under the Sanguine Shields sodality.
t.Bregasland: The conjunction to stop the Burhfæst was not taken, so the Jotun established it in Gravenmarch and Svynna of Ldansk still lives.
t.Brocéliande: The Spear of the Seven investigated the mystery of Starstrand Steading in Boar's Dell, with the outcome known only to Corwyn Heartsbane.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Casinea were tagged in the As it is when it was winds of magic entry.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the When the River Rises wind included some discussion of the newly liberated Feroz.
t.Forest of Ulnak: At Varnalis' Cache in Grimfen Mire, heralds of Surut and Druj were defeated and 16 wains of white granite were delivered to Hugh Farrier.
t.Hahnmark: Tobrytan Dunning's band defeated the scions at Dun's Reach in Wood Heath.
t.Kahraman: The wild Scorrero rose in Kahraman in response to powerful Imperial magic and swept south towards Segura and Madruga.
t.Kallavesa: Ishal mystics sought new magical protections for Kallavesa, as Dripping Echoes of the Fen is no longer as effective as it once was.
t.Karov: The Deadwood Knight, also called the Schlacta of Rot, gathered strength in the wild places of southern Karov.
t.Madruga: The Scorrero flood cleansed Madruga of the Blight and the Dry Patricians but brought destruction with it. Governor Rahab was assassinated, Dry Patricians were defeated on the Great Grasses, and wreckers were killed in Calvos Sound.
t.Mareave: Eilian Sweetwater's appraisal found expensive ways to deal with at least two of the three uncooperative southern regions, and further investment opportunities were offered.
t.Miekarova: The Master of Ice and Darkness's band defeated the scions at Biljana's Sward in Srodkoja.
t.Mitwold: Urse Longarm was slain at Jenny's Copse and ghosts were exorcised at Halebale Farm, while Faraden involvement in the recent attack on Meade strained relations.
t.Morrow: The attempt to kill the Druj and rescue Megaris Sunspire at the Still Glade in Peregro failed with significant Imperial casualties.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos remained annoyed over Imperial involvement in the failure of its joint venture with the Grendel here, and a report from Tsark was summarised.
t.Mournwold: Naomi of Virtue's Rest travelled under a flag of truce to speak with the Jotun in Mournwold, and ghosts were exorcised at the Glen of Red Shadow in Southmoor.
t.Necropolis: The Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic's band defeated wreckers at the Grove of Silence in Longbeach and rescued Kauitalic.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the civil service summarised the Empire's latest report from Otkodov.
t.Redoubt: Scions were defeated at the Tilphussian Pass in Naris with some Imperial casualties, and Grendel and Asavean forces were beaten at Lucia's Holt in Siluri.
t.Sarvos: Controversy grew over Sarcophan law and a planned blasphemous cathedral on the nearby Alivetti estates as the Vandersaar sought further investment. Wreckers were stopped in Bocche.
t.Segura: The risen Scorrero swept through Segura on its way from Kahraman to Madruga.
t.Sermersuaq: Jotun were killed and Big and Little Icebarn dealt with in the Suaq Wastes, and Maarik the Golden Tongue was killed at Aino's Rest in the Silver Peaks.
t.Skallahn: The Champion of Ambition's band defeated the Jotun at Auguaard's Bluff and delivered 14 wains of weirwood to Eldrid Vestardottir.
t.Spiral: Two bands rescued all the threatened citizens near Harrier's Nest in Screed.
t.Temeschwar: The Ratkings guild brought the city's rat plague under control, but something malign remains, and conjunctions in Hanuri sought answers.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens remained tense, its fate torn between the Dawnish Assembly and senators, though Druj and heralds of Surut were defeated in the Bleaks.
t.Therunin: Lofyn Blood-cloak's force slowed the Druj advance at Tarn Bend, but the concoctions of the Sephals Cauldron were unleashed on Lower Tarn Valley.
t.Weirwater: The Deadwood Knight gathered strength in northern Weirwater ahead of an attack on Dawn, and the planned academy at Sandling remained uncommissioned.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: Grendel and Asaveans were defeated at Dunreagh's Brush, and 12 wains of mithril were delivered to Delora i Sol-Devorador i Erigo.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: With the conjunction at Rock Foot Wood not taken, the Jotun Burhfæst was established here and Svynna of Ldansk survived.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The mystery of Starstrand Steading was investigated by the Spear of the Seven, with results known to Corwyn Heartsbane.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: Druj and heralds of Surut were defeated at Varnalis' Cache, and its stockpile of 16 wains of white granite was claimed.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Scions were defeated at Dun's Reach by Tobrytan Dunning's band.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: the Grimir of Wittal Grove was among those tagged in the Rising in Runegrott wind.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The Custodian of the Lost investigated events at Gorek's Hollow, with the outcome known to Anthemius Netherwatch.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Tabhorios was revealed to have joined the Children of Wrecks, and all the wreckers at the Orchard of Tabhorios were killed.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Champion of Vigilance investigated the Baleen Cave, with results known to Jared.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn was one of three southern regions whose uncooperative orc inhabitants Eilian Sweetwater's costly appraisal sought to address.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal's recalcitrant inhabitants were among those the Mareave appraisal examined, with expensive options found for at least two of the three regions.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Fleisardh's uncooperative inhabitants were a subject of the appraisal, which also offered insight into why they resist Imperial rule.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: Scions were defeated at Biljana's Sward by the Master of Ice and Darkness's band.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Urse Longarm and the other Jotun were killed at Jenny's Copse.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: All the ghosts at Halebale Farm were exorcised.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The effort to kill the Druj at the Still Glade suffered significant Imperial casualties, and Megaris Sunspire was not recovered.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The Friar of Honour's Rest tracked down the ghosts at the Glen of Red Shadow, and all were exorcised.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Wreckers were defeated at the Grove of Silence and Kauitalic was rescued.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Scions were defeated at the Tilphussian Pass, with some Imperial casualties.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: Grendel and Asavean forces were defeated at Lucia's Holt.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The Jade Custodian's band prevented a ritual at Ferocity's Stand and killed all the wreckers.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: A debate between the self-professed best in the world was held at the Solare Estate, with the outcome known to Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra and Marta i Guerra.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Maarik the Golden Tongue was killed at Aino's Rest.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Jotun were killed and both Big Icebarn and Little Icebarn were dealt with at the Howling Steppe and the Desolate Tarn.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Jotun were defeated at Auguaard's Bluff, and 14 wains of weirwood were delivered.
r.Spiral/Screed: All the citizens near Harrier's Nest were rescued in two separate missions.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Senator for Temeschwar met the Rat Kings guild at Terrier's Roar, and the Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind sought Brinton von Temeschwar at the Old Priory; both outcomes are known only to those involved.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Knight-protector of Winter's band defeated Druj and heralds of Surut at the Hollow Tree.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Druj advance was slowed at Tarn Bend, but the concoctions of the Sephals Cauldron were unleashed on the region.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: The academy honouring Ozren de Orzel at Belletain has yet to be commissioned, and the Vardas crisis will block any profound effects of its consecration until resolved.

386YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: Asavean ships raided Meade in Mitwold. War broke out over Madruga and Feroz, where the Children of Wrecks had seized the islands. The Tusks led an Imperial push against the Jotun, who had taken Sarcombe in Southmoor. The Druj poisoned Therunin and were rumoured to be meddling with the vallorn, while three Imperial armies marched from Mareave into the Petrified Forest of Ayereed. The Military Council would choose two of three battles: against the Children of Wrecks at Free Landing, the Jotun in the Ore Hills, or the Druj in Sweetglades. Numerous conjunctions were listed across the Empire, along with each nation's force weight and standing military considerations.

n.Dawn: Dawn brought a force weight of 58 to the battle opportunities, its armies still barred from Cautious Advance and Give Ground. Its heroes were called to conjunctions against Druj ritualists in the Barrens and the Speakers of Famine in Astolat.
n.Druj: The Druj invaded Therunin, poisoning the soil and slaughtering humans and orcs alike, with rumours that they sought to tamper with the slumbering vallorn. They faced a possible battle in Sweetglades and conjunctions in Peakedge Song and the Barrens.
n.Grendel: The Grendel faced war on two fronts: the struggle over Feroz and Madruga in 'Glass and flame', and three Imperial armies driving into their Ayereed homelands in 'Steel and salt'.
n.Highguard: Highguard offered a force weight of 21, and the Kruidenkenner Trademaster was named to lead a conjunction against wreckers at Longbeach in Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs contributed a force weight of 5 to the battle opportunities, and their armies could still take the Forge Hammers order in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Having taken Sarcombe in Southmoor in the summer, the Jotun now faced an Imperial drive led by the Tusks to push them out of the Mournwold. They also faced a possible battle in the Ore Hills and several conjunctions, including one to stop them slaughtering the Feni in Bregasland.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Therunin was invaded and poisoned by the Druj, and its striders and steadings rose to resist in 'Blood and mire'. Navarr brought the largest force weight of all, 61, and was called to a conjunction in Miaren against followers of the Braying Lord.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast suffered on the Bay of Catazar: Siroc had been burned, the Children of Wrecks held Madruga's islands and Feroz remained under Governor Rahab. The Freeborn offered a force weight of 19, and the Hand of Guerra was named to lead a conjunction against wreckers in Calvos Sound.
n.The League: The League brought a force weight of 21, and its cities faced conjunctions in Holberg, Tassato, Sarvos, Spiral and Temeschwar, including one to slay the Braying Lord in Vardstein Vale.
n.The Marches: The Marches endured an Asavean raid on Meade and torrential rains that threatened the harvest, while the Tusks led the push against the Jotun in Mournwold. Marcher armies kept their home-territory strength bonuses, and the nation brought a force weight of 30.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was named to lead a small conjunction investigating the situation at a mine shaft in Thule-held Nithoggir.
n.Urizen: Urizen brought a force weight of 13, and the Churnspire Adjutor was named to lead a conjunction against the Shuddering Wrast in Morrow.
n.Varushka: Varushka brought a force weight of 15 but still generated fewer victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies. It was called to conjunctions to soothe the wolves of Nadezhdikov in Volodmartz and to make the vale of Bulgakov in Karov habitable.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark brought a force weight of 59, and its armies kept their Fight with Honour order and their special modifiers against the Jotun. Its heroes were called to conjunctions against the Crimson Band in Hahnmark and against Asaveans threatening the Pilgrim's Trail in Kallavesa.

t.Astolat: A conjunction was offered at the Grand Spinney in Winterbourne to kill the Speakers of Famine, with Jared of the Sentinels Tower named as responsible.
t.Ayereed: Three Imperial armies advanced south from Mareave into Ayereed's Petrified Forest to conquer the Grendel homelands. A conjunction was also offered in Cornaghan to stop the Asaveans reinforcing Stormlords Rise.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: storms continued to wrack the Bay, and the Brass Coast was said to suffer there amid the war over Madruga and Feroz.
t.Bregasland: Imperial armies could Billet in Bregasland, and the Strong Reeds kept their bonus there. A conjunction was offered in the Grey Fens to stop the Jotun slaughtering the Feni.
t.Feroz: Long under the heel of Governor Rahab, Feroz was one of the fronts in the war chronicled in 'Glass and flame'.
t.Hahnmark: A conjunction was offered at the Tainted Bawn in Wood Heath to kill the Crimson Band, under the oversight of the Imperial Huntsmarshall.
t.Holberg: A small conjunction was offered at the Wunderkind Fields in Holmaeur to kill the Feasters of Marrow, assigned to the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage.
t.Kallavesa: A conjunction was offered at Ardith's Holt in the West Marsh to protect the Pilgrim's Trail from the Asaveans, assigned to the Speaker of the Crows.
t.Karov: A series of short conjunctions was offered at Bulgakov in Duzekani to make the vale habitable, under the Grieftender of the Forgotten.
t.Madruga: With Siroc burned and the islands seized by the Children of Wrecks, Madruga became a battleground. It hosted a possible battle at Free Landing to break the Gathering Storm and a conjunction against wreckers in Calvos Sound.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Mareave was the starting point for the three Imperial armies marching south into Ayereed.
t.Miaren: A large conjunction was offered at the Soured Pasture in Goldglades to kill the followers of the Braying Lord, assigned to the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield.
t.Mitwold: Asavean ships made a surprise raid on Meade, Mitwold's market town, in 'Harvest of infamy'. Imperial armies could Billet there, and the Drakes kept their bonus when fighting in Mitwold.
t.Morrow: A conjunction was offered at Iulia's Grove in Peregro to kill the Shuddering Wrast. Highborn and Urizen defenders in Morrow retained their bonus against attacks from Zenith.
t.Mournwold: The Empire, led by the Tusks, moved to drive out the Jotun who had taken Sarcombe in Southmoor. Mournwold hosted a possible battle in the Ore Hills and several conjunctions in Southmoor and the Chalkdowns.
t.Necropolis: A conjunction was offered at the Magazjin Plain in Longbeach to kill wreckers, assigned to the Kruidenkenner Trademaster.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan armies could still take the Hospitality of the Boyars order in Ossium.
t.Otkodov: A small, longer conjunction was offered at Shaft #3 in Skarlans, Nithoggir, to investigate the situation, assigned to the Ambassador to Otkodov.
t.Sarvos: A conjunction was offered to protect the Isle of the Fox in Uccelini, assigned to the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Asavean ships sailed through the Sea of Snow and down the Gullet to raid the Marches.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Orc armies could still take the Forge Hammers order in Skarsind.
t.Spiral: A conjunction was offered at Eammon's Bawn in Apulus to stop the Wailing Gyre, assigned to the Senator for Spiral.
t.Tassato: A conjunction was offered in the Felladonni Woods of Tassato Mestra to stop a warband claiming ilium, assigned to the Tassatan Hills title.
t.Temeschwar: A large conjunction was offered at the Putrid Fields in Vardstein Vale to slay the Braying Lord, assigned to the Delver of the Depths.
t.The Barrens: A conjunction was offered at Skrengal Copse in the Untrod Groves to kill Druj ritualists, assigned to the Knight-protector of Spring.
t.Therunin: The Druj invaded Therunin, spreading poison through the soil and pools, and were rumoured to be meddling with the slumbering vallorn. The territory hosted a possible battle in Sweetglades and a conjunction in Peakedge Song.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies could Billet in Upwold, and the Bounders kept their strength bonus there.
t.Volodmartz: A conjunction was offered in the Choked Forest of Perumaki to soothe the wolves of Nadezhdikov, assigned to the Grim Gardener.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a standing rule gave Highborn or Urizen armies attacking into Zenith from Morrow a bonus to territory captured.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: Imperial heroes were called to the Grand Spinney to kill the Speakers of Famine.
r.Ayereed/Cornaghan: A conjunction at Anabla's Orchard sought to stop the Asaveans reinforcing Stormlords Rise, under the General of the Seventh Wave.
r.Ayereed/Petrified Forest: Three Imperial armies advanced into this dry and dangerous region from Mareave.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A conjunction at Hal's Hollow sought to stop the Jotun slaughtering the Feni, under the Imperial Advisor for the Feni.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: A conjunction at the Tainted Bawn targeted the Crimson Band.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A conjunction at Ardith's Holt sought to protect the Pilgrim's Trail from the Asaveans.
r.Karov/Duzekani: Repeated small conjunctions to the vale of Bulgakov aimed to make it habitable.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A conjunction on Santana's Path aimed to kill the wreckers, under the Hand of Guerra.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Freeborn Plain was the site of a possible Saturday battle against the Children of Wrecks to break the Gathering Storm.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: A conjunction at the Soured Pasture targeted the followers of the Braying Lord.
r.Morrow/Peregro: A conjunction at Iulia's Grove aimed to kill the Shuddering Wrast.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Two conjunctions were offered here: one to investigate a disturbance at Tilly's Howe, and one to defeat the Jotun at the Broken Corral.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Jade Wood was the site of a possible battle against the Jotun to rouse the Mourn's defenders, with Stephen of Sarcombe's warband fighting alongside the orcs.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Seized by the Jarl of Jarls along with Sarcombe in the summer, Southmoor saw conjunctions to kill Dalton Royse at Charlie's Coppice and to clear the last Jotun cache at Fecund Boscage.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: A conjunction on the Magazjin Plain aimed to kill wreckers.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: A small conjunction to Shaft #3 at Skarlans was offered to investigate the situation.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: A conjunction aimed to protect the Isle of the Fox.
r.Spiral/Apulus: A conjunction at Eammon's Bawn aimed to stop the Wailing Gyre.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: A conjunction in the Felladonni Woods sought to stop a warband claiming ilium.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: The largest Friday conjunction, at the Putrid Fields, aimed to slay the Braying Lord.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: A conjunction at Bronwen's Stand aimed to stop the Druj, under the Eastern Broker.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Ashborder was the site of a possible Sunday battle to stop the Druj's plan.

A challenging time.d: Barien could not respond to Challenge the Iron Duke because of an ongoing conjunction, so his heralds offered alternatives. Citizens without Imperial titles gathered favours by fighting one another in Anvil. Twenty-four competitors then fought a grand melee at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael, Miaren, for the sword Pinnacle. The sword may be borne until the holder dies or gains an Imperial title. Jacques Flayer of Dawn won. Past victors of Dawn and Wintermark were summoned to the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure, Semmerholm, where a year-long challenge between the two nations was set, to end the following Autumn. Brynell Goldengrove, acting for the Archmage of Summer, raised a declaration of amity naming the Clattering Curtain's performing arts competition at the Winter Solstice to receive Barien's prize.

n.Dawn: Dawn's past victors of the Iron Duke's challenges were invited to a year-long contest against Wintermark, and Jacques Flayer of Dawn won the Pinnacle Tourney and the sword Pinnacle.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Pinnacle Tourney was held via conjunction at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael, a region of the Navarr-held territory of Miaren.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story follows a League street gang, the Mudskippers, racing across the Sarvos docks.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's past victors, including Artis Greyholm and Tarik of Ashenhall, were summoned to receive a year-long challenge pitting them against Dawn, to be concluded at the following Autumn Equinox.

t.Miaren: Miaren hosted the Pinnacle Tourney, a grand melee fought via conjunction at Goldenoak Circle in Serenael.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story is set at the Sarvos docks, where the Mudskippers hold their annual Buskin's Day race.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's Grove of the Thousand hosted Barien's usual rewards ceremony and the setting of the Victor's Challenge between Dawn and Wintermark.

r.Miaren/Serenael: Goldenoak Circle in Serenael was the site of the Pinnacle Tourney, which was open to spectators and won by Jacques Flayer of Dawn.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: At the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure, Barien's heralds set the year-long Victor's Challenge for the invited victors of Dawn and Wintermark.

A stone for a stone.d: Naomi consulted Marcher orcs, studied past wars and crossed under truce to speak with the Jotun in Mournwold. She traced their enmity to the abrogated ceasefire and the Mournwold curses, after which the Jotun refused peace until every dishonoured warrior, above all Jarl Haakon, was dead. Her suggested steps were to kill Haakon, avoid further atrocities, start another war or inflict a major defeat, agree terms for war, build a new Meeting Place, echo Jotun gests, and resolve Jotun hatred of the Navarr. The Lasambrians offered a 'Little Sibling' ceasefire in exchange for Gambit and Serra Damata, or a 'Big Sibling' secession. Their delegation came to Anvil, but no treaty went before the Senate.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is cited as an example of land a nation regards as its own, and the Lasambrians are likened to the Dawnish in their keenness for adventure.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun insult the Navarr as 'human Druj', and the Druj are named among the enemies who would exploit any Imperial weakness.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named among the foes who would press a weakened Empire, and as having helped a third of the Lasambrians flee to the Broken Shore.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian envoys are likened to the Highborn in spirituality, and travelled with Naomi along the road towards Casinea.
n.Jotun: The appraisal found the Jotun bound by faith to seek worthy war and unwilling to make peace until Jarl Haakon and the other warriors dishonoured in the Mournwold are slain. Even then, any peace would likely be used to rebuild or to attack the Faraden, while the Lasambrian Jotun pursued their own deals.
n.Navarr: The Jotun despise the Navarr as 'human Druj' and give them no quarter. Naomi suggested either improving that view through diplomacy or keeping Navarr armies away from Jotun campaigns, which would be hard if war reached Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn have won Jotun respect, notably for raising a barrow over the dead of Fort Braydon and through Avisena, the 'Golden Jarl'. The Lasambrian Little Sibling deal would cede two Kahraman regions in return for keeping all Jotun armies out of Freeborn territory for two years.
n.The Marches: Naomi consulted Marcher orcs, and noted lingering Marcher resentment over the Mournwold curses. She also found that the Jotun respect the Marchers to a lesser degree than Wintermark and the Freeborn.
n.Thule: Starting a war with the Thule was put forward as something that might prompt the Jotun to grant a temporary peace, though Naomi warned it could be cataclysmic without other steps. Guntherm's past alliance with the Jotun against the Thule was recalled as a precedent.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's choice to fight with honour, as in retaking Sermersuaq, earned the Jotun's respect but no interest in a ceasefire. Naomi advised that at least one Wintermark army fight honourably in every Jotun campaign to avoid accidental dishonour.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: used as an analogy for how deeply the Jotun regard their claimed lands as their own.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay is not named; the page notes only the Jotun dislike of open water and dread of drowning.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: resentment over the Mournwold curses is said to linger in Bregasland.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian delegation travelled with Naomi along the road to Casinea before turning off for Anvil.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians are noted to have attacked Feroz in the past.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Jotun claim, at least in part, as their own.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: a sept in Tromsa claims Hercynia's woods and peaks were its domain before the Terunael came.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman, where the Jotun were defeated at Fort Braydon, is claimed by both Jotun and Lasambrians. It was the subject of the Little Sibling offer to cede Gambit and Serra Damata, and Naomi met the Lasambrians near its border on the Scorrero River.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: listed among the lands the Lasambrians lay claim to.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Jotun claim as their own.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Naomi warned that keeping the Navarr from fighting the Jotun would be fraught if the war moved to Liathaven.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun-claimed lands, and as an example of land the Marchers see as theirs.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold curses, which killed nearly one in six inhabitants, left the Jotun dishonoured and committed to war until Jarl Haakon, its former ruler, is dead. Naomi made her truce visit to the Jotun there.
t.Reinos: Reinos is claimed in part by the Lasambrians, and Naomi met them where its border meets Kahraman and Segura. Under the Little Sibling offer, no Imperial army would enter Reinos for two years.
t.Segura: Segura is claimed by both Jotun and Lasambrians, and its former senator Avisena is revered by the Jotun as the Golden Jarl. It would be covered by the Little Sibling ceasefire barring Jotun armies from Freeborn lands.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq is claimed by the Jotun. Wintermark's honourable campaign to retake it saw the Jotun allow Imperial forces to recover their wounded and dead.
t.Tromsa: Imperial generals chose not to attack Mount Majastind during their invasion of Tromsa, which may have been pivotal in improving Jotun views of the nations involved.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Gambit was one of the two regions the Lasambrians asked the Empire to cede to them under the proposed Little Sibling ceasefire. No treaty was brought before the Senate.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Serra Damata was proposed for cession under the Little Sibling deal, which would have handed the Lasambrians the Damatian Cliffs and the Red Depths. No treaty was brought before the Senate.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Mount Majastind, believed to hold Ulven's bones and at least three powerful artefacts, is the Jotun's most sacred site. The Imperial decision to spare it may have been the most important step in changing Jotun views.

A victory for diplomacy.d: Ambassador Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo's treaty gave the Iron Confederacy Free Trade status and criminalised the export of narcotics to it for three years. In response, Duke Helen Gerradin of Veroigne allowed Imperial fleets at Robec to receive Kobol's Vigour, a metallic elixir, in place of luxuries. The Dukes declined a joint campaign against the Children of Wrecks, recalling that their offer to invade Feroz had been rebuffed. They also urged the Empire to disband the Conclave and Synod to oppose Dumon, which the Empire declined. Ser Marquette Lavasse, Temple of the Veiled King priests and Baron de Bestel's kin visited Anvil. Afterwards Robec granted Imperial merchants mercantilist status, though scrutiny and some delays remained.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as believed members of the Freedom Accord and fellow victims of the Children of Wrecks, and the Suranni asked for evidence of the claim that the pirates were brought by 'the Asaveans and their Grendel pawns'.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo, as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, drove the treaty and hosted the Suranni delegations. Suranni merchants mostly travel overland through the Brass Coast, so they benefit from the tariff-free trade.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay. It describes the Children of Wrecks' piracy against the Empire and the Grendel, and the Suranni intention to guard only their own territorial waters.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, and particularly the town of Bramar, was once a favoured Suranni market before it was lost. The Empire's rebuff of a Suranni offer to invade Feroz is cited as the reason the Dukes refused a military alliance.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura is where Iron Confederacy merchants most often sell their goods, now without tariffs on their imports.
t.Veroigne: Duke Helen Gerradin welcomed the narcotics ban for her port of Robec and allowed Imperial fleets there to receive Kobol's Vigour. After the delegation's visit, sanctions on Imperial merchants at Robec were lifted, though some delays and scrutiny remained.

All the way to Anvil.d: Alexandre Sortilega di Apulian, who fronts the Company of the Venturesome Harrier's tours of the Black Plateau, came with a reckoner to confront the League assembly over its denunciation. Isaziah, a Highborn merrow, returned with an incense made from Tamarbodian mushrooms. The Sagrado sutannir offered up to 50 people a glimpse of a past life through true liao infused by Sung. A grieving Highborn pilgrim sought tombola participants. Rahuun Amahuz, a former Grendel magician now in Apulus, sought a 'friend of Melissa'. An Axou merchant sought discreet physicks for three patients. A herald of Tharim was to address the Navarr about the vallorn. Valja Nikodemin Kopec sought volunteers to cleanse Bulgakov, and Megan Brownblood came to question the vines.

n.Grendel: Rahuun Amahuz, a former Grendel orc magician, had defected with half the Black Sand Circle to the League, and boasted of ties to a Grendel Wind Lord he was careful not to contact for fear of treason accusations.
n.Highguard: Two Highborn visitors were expected: the merrow Isaziah, bringing a mushroom incense to test and sell, and the grieving grey pilgrim Tamar, who blamed the tombola's mountebanks for the loss of a brother.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: their egregore received no invitation to the Sagrado true liao offering, as Imperial Orcs cannot benefit from liao in any form.
n.Navarr: The Autocrator of the Sheathed Armoury was due at the Navarr camp to explain how Tharim, Surut or Skathe might aid the campaign against the vallorn, while Megan Brownblood came to demand the vines' answers on their oath.
n.The League: The League assembly faced an incensed Alexandre Sortilega di Apulian, who threatened a defamation suit over its denunciation of the Black Plateau tours, and Apulus had gained Rahuun Amahuz's Circle of Black Sand as a new guild.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the astronomancers of the Circle of Black Sand now rub shoulders with Urizen students of the stars, and Zenith's spires were once visited by Axou seeking medicine.

t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Beoraidh half of the Black Sand Circle, under Mannun Amahuz, kept the coven's ritual library after the split.
t.Miaren: The Thrice-Cursed Court's message arrived through a straining winter regio near Seren, from which a vate returned bearing the Bound King's scroll.
t.Reikos: The peculiar mushrooms of Tamarbode were the source of Isaziah's distilled substance and her new incense, brought to Anvil for testing and sale.
t.Spiral: The Company of the Venturesome Harrier's walking tours across benighted Spiral and the Black Plateau, branded a scam by the League's priests, were at the centre of Alexandre's dispute.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the learned halls of Tassato Regario were once a destination for Axou seeking medical knowledge.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the high spires of Zenith were once visited by Axou seeking medical learning.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is home to the Black Sand Circle half led by Mannun Amahuz, who took the coven's ritual library there.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Odd mushrooms harvested in Tamarbode underpin Isaziah's continuing experiments and the incense she planned to test and sell at Anvil.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Rahuun Amahuz had settled in Apulus, set up the Circle of Black Sand as a guild in the League city and styled himself its Merchant-Prince.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Mentioned in passing: its learned halls were among the places Axou once visited for medicine, a practice not resumed since contact was restored.

As it is when it was.d: A magnitude-50 Summer enchantment showed a glowing winged figure over Casinea, drawing complaints of waste and idolatry. Valasheim's forgemistress sought an apprentice from twelve runesmiths. Thornsong House was completed in Therunin, and its first Thornsinger was to choose a potion for research. The last trods were restored, and Liathaven's Wither the Seed curse was found to have ended. Senate-commissioned Journeymage Towers let the Wavewatchers contain Dho'uala. The Thule enchanted their forts in Imperial lands ahead of an ambassadorial meeting. Lashonar's feathers would carry letters to the Night realm. Conjunctions arose at Tilly's Howe and in the Choked Forest. Sanvar Isk was humiliated by Tassato's orphans.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: pessimistic Navarr note that Thornsong House would be moot if the Druj conquered Therunin, which seems very unlikely.
n.Highguard: Highborn in Casinea largely disliked the winged sky-figure, complaining of lost sleep and wasted mana. Some priests questioned whether it was idolatry and suggested the Imperial Censor consider a Conclave interdiction.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Thule fort of Crow's Keep, on Crow's Ridge in Skarsind, now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.
n.Jotun: The curse on Liathaven, which they call Ashvale, has ended, and some vates suspect northern Jotun who heed Wise Rangara of helping the Feni. The Jotun will likely need their own plans to deal with the Feni and the reawakened vallorn.
n.Navarr: Thornsong House was completed, and Navarr herb garden owners would choose the first Thornsinger by Tally of the Votes. The trods were fully restored, but the curse their nation placed on Liathaven has been lifted.
n.The League: In Tassato, Sanvar Isk was fooled and fined after the Church of the Little Mother's orphans tricked him. League mountebanks are also being recruited into the Wavewatchers around the Semmerlak.
n.The Marches: Marchers left behind in Jotun-occupied Mournwold report disappearances and hooded figures near Tilly's Howe, where a conjunction was found. Marchers bordering Liathaven also suggested the Spymaster Bernard Dugdale rebuild a spy network there.
n.Thule: The Thule laid powerful enchantments on all their forts in Imperial regions: ice giants, pale flame, white wolves from Sorin's court and Autumn runes. This appeared to be a show of strength before talks with the Ambassador to Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the nationwide efforts of the Urizen, overseen by the Doyen of the Spires, are listed as one of the Empire's colleges of magic.
n.Varushka: Volhov joined the new Wavewatchers with the Wise assembly's blessing, and the trods in Volodmartz and Karov had been restored. The wolves of Nadezhdikov have risen in Volodmartz, and Thule forts in Varushkan lands now bear striking enchantments.
n.Wintermark: Valasheim's forgemistress Ursula Starhammer invited twelve egregore-divined runesmiths to compete to become her apprentice. Meanwhile the Thule citadel in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks has been reinforced by ice giants.

t.Casinea: A glowing winged figure resembling Umbar i Elba Stardo i Guerra appeared in the sky, clearest above Anvil, and faded over the season. It provoked complaints of noise, waste and possible idolatry.
t.Hahnmark: At Valasheim in Valasmark, the forge of the Aflhal sought a new apprentice through a conjunction challenge during the summit.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its trods, rent by the Cold Sun's servants, are noted as having been restored at the Spring Equinox.
t.Karsk: The Thule fort of Krevsatyzmei in Krevsaty is now attended by great white wolves, apparently gifts from Sorin's court.
t.Liathaven: The Wither the Seed curse has ended, so humans and orcs there can bear children again. It also means nothing now holds the vallorn quiescent, and citizens suggested rebuilding an Imperial spy network.
t.Miaren: The trods torn apart by the Cold Sun's scions were repaired at the Summer Solstice, though some paths have shifted slightly.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: it is not named; the link is the Wavewatchers' recruitment of Varushkan volhov from around the Semmerlak.
t.Mournwold: A conjunction to Tilly's Howe in the Chalk Downs, contested with the Jotun, was found after reports of disappearances and robed figures near a dolmen. It appears to call for investigation and magic rather than violence.
t.Ossium: The Thule fort of Flajajokep in the Bonewood is covered in glowing Autumn runes, and heralds of two Autumn cities attend its markets.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as masters of Otkodov, and its Imperial ambassador Kindra Surefoot is due to meet the Thule Ambassador.
t.Sermersuaq: The Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone in the Silver Peaks has been reinforced by ice giants, presumably called from Cathan Canae.
t.Skarsind: The Thule fort of Crow's Keep on Crow's Ridge now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.
t.Tassato: Sanvar Isk was tricked by the Church of the Little Mother's orphans, then fined and thrown out by a magistrate. The Church planned to meet interested parties at Anvil before he auctions access to the Loom of Spells.
t.The Semmerlak: The completed Journeymage Towers let the Wavewatchers counter the sovereign Dho'uala's threat to shipping. Dho'uala is still awake, and the lake's ilium and fish remain an open problem.
t.Therunin: Thornsong House, the college of herbalism, was completed, and its Thornsinger will direct a year-long potion research project. Navarr worry about protecting the house from the vallorn.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: it is not named; the closest link is the note that some northern Jotun seek Wise Rangara's counsel.
t.Volodmartz: The wolves of Nadezhdikov have risen in the Choked Forest near the Gardens of the Grim, and the Grim Gardener is responsible for soothing them. Its trods were also restored in Spring.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: The Aflhal forge at Valasheim will host a challenge to choose Ursula Starhammer's new apprentice, reached by conjunction during the summit.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule fort of Krevsatyzmei is now attended by great white wolves from Sorin's court.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: last summer's giant sky-miner over the Ore Hills, which Marchers treated as an excuse for a picnic, is cited as an earlier comparison.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Flajajokep bears glowing Autumn runes, and unusual numbers of Autumn heralds attend its markets.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The garrison of the Citadel of Silver and Bone has been reinforced by ice giants.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Keep now burns night and day with a pale red-green flame.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: Navarr warn that if the Greenheart is triggered, vallornspawn could threaten Thornsong House and Peakedge Song.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are urged to consider how Peakedge Song, along with Thornsong House, will be protected if the Greenheart is triggered.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: Mentioned in passing: it is not named on the page; the only link is the note about northern Jotun seeking Wise Rangara's counsel.

Authority and acceptance.d: The Senate's Summer renunciation of six northern regions satisfied Rak, who invited Ambassador Kindra Surefoot to a private parley on the Thule treaty, which expires in Summer 387YE. A conjunction to a Five Fang Consortium site in Otkodov opened. Skoura welcomed the new treaty and sent delegations about a schema and the Eoradal aqueduct. Tsark returned memory-stripped Urizeni prisoners through Occursion and sent envoys to Anvil. Asavea's bounty on Imperial-bound shipping cost the treasury 62 thrones. Thirty Asavean priests surrendered at Oran. Jarm welcomed the ban on mercenaries aiding the Commonwealth, but the Conclave refused Brotherhood of Tian, so Measure was lost. Speaker Morna of the Grendel declined to attend Anvil.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Consul who handles Skoura and Tsark, Lord Jarrigk Orzel, is of Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as a bordering orc nation, a past target of Thule cooperation, and invaders whose attack shocks the returning Urizeni.
n.Grendel: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire, with Asavean support, and are pressing hard in Feroz and Ayereed. Speaker Morna declined to attend Anvil until there is something of substance to discuss, such as the Children of Wrecks.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark delegation travels west toward Casinea to reach Anvil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc interest in rebuilding the Skouran aqueduct in Eoradal prompted a Skouran delegation, which asked to meet Legion Engineer Groza and Senator Gaddak of Mareave about the water it would carry.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as a bordering orc nation and a past target of Imperial–Thule cooperation.
n.Navarr: The Tsark sages Apollion and Kristoph particularly hoped to meet Navarr guides during their visit to Anvil.
n.The Brass Coast: The three Freeborn generals had to decide whether to execute or repatriate around thirty Asavean priests who surrendered to them at Oran. Freeborn ambassadors handled both Asavea and the Grendel.
n.The League: The Tsark envoys were especially keen to meet the League, whom they understood now to rule Spiral, home to some of the returned prisoners.
n.Thule: Satisfied by the Senate's renunciation of claims, Rak invited the Empire's ambassador to negotiate the expiring treaty, expecting a further price for peace. He also confirmed that Gisli Baerson funded Otkodov's famine relief.
