n.Urizen: Urizeni long held prisoner on Zabor returned to Zenith with their memories of Tsark removed, bringing the body of Ursula. Quinta, who chose to stay in Tsark, travelled to explain that choice to the Urizeni at Anvil.
n.Varushka: Varushkan ambassador Nikita Teanga Volkov handled the frosty relations with Jarm. The Senate's renunciation recognised Miechernya, Krevsaty, Bonewood and Webwood as part of Otkodov.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot was invited to a private parley with Rak on the treaty's future, and the Tsark envoys hoped to meet Wintermark mediators.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are reported to be heavily engaged in Ayereed.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Asavean vessels will not enter the Bay, where Imperial and Grendel ships skirmish amid the Children of Wrecks.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark delegation sets off west toward Casinea on its way to Anvil.
t.Feroz: The Grendel have struck decisively into Feroz, and Asavean priests who surrendered after the siege of Oran are held under guard there while the Freeborn generals decide their fate.
t.Karsk: The Senate's renunciation recognised Krevsaty in Karsk as part of Otkodov, now and forever.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a major Grendel force of armies and navies is believed still to be in Madruga, though scrying there is difficult.
t.Mareave: A Skouran schema found in Mareave was to be collected by a Skouran representative. Skoura weighed whether to supply water through a rebuilt aqueduct in Eoradal.
t.Miekarova: The Senate's renunciation recognised Miechernya in Miekarova as part of Otkodov.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Tsark released Urizeni prisoners from Zabor and, after debating its isolation, sent Sage Apollion, Sage Kristoph and Quinta to Anvil to learn about the Imperial nations.
t.Ossium: Ossium, conquered with Thule cooperation, saw its Bonewood and Webwood recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
t.Otkodov: A conjunction opened to a Five Fang Consortium venture in Otkodov while treaty talks loomed. Rak confirmed Gisli Baerson's funds had eased Otkodov's famine.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's Gaze fortification stands in Lustri on the border between Zenith and the Sarangrave.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq, liberated with Thule help, had its Silver Peaks recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
t.Skarsind: The Senate's renunciation recognised Crow's Ridge in Skarsind as part of Otkodov.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: some returned prisoners originally came from Spiral, and the Tsark know it is now ruled by the League.
t.Zenith: Former Urizeni prisoners and Tsark envoys came down into Zenith and were received at the Temple of the Wanderer, where the returnees were sheltered while they reconnected with the world.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Krevsaty was among the regions the Senate recognised as part of Otkodov, the statement the Thule demanded before reopening talks.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The ruined Skouran aqueduct in Eoradal, which the Imperial Orcs hope to rebuild, prompted Skoura to send engineers to discuss how much water arid Eoradal would need.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov, now and forever.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Bonewood was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Webwood was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: The Sentinel Gate opened to Shaft #3, Skarlans, in Nithoggir, apparently linked to the Five Fang Consortium venture, with violence considered possible but unlikely.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks were recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge was recognised by the Senate as part of Otkodov.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's Gaze was built in Lustri two years earlier after the Senate declined Tsark's offer of help.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Returning Urizeni and Tsark cuvari came through Mislitel Pass into Occursion and were received at Cato Hypation's Temple of the Wanderer, carrying Ursula's body.

Beneath mithril spires.d: Commonwealth siege engineer Poldi Hellebrant praised the new embassy and docks under construction at Hedra in Necropolis, though she worried about Jarmish and Commonwealth ships sharing the Couros river. The war with Jarm over Lantir is expected to be long. Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen regretted the Senate's refusal to let captains fight Jarm, thanked the Empire for gifts of mana, and dismissed concerns about the Freedom Accord. The Commonwealth tactfully declined to approve contact with the Viyerda. The Asavean bounty has cut Commonwealth shipping, which boosts Imperial fleets trading there. The Senate raised no motions on the Viyerda or on exploring the Sea of Steel, and enthusiasm for exploration faded.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their armies are used as a yardstick for the scale of the Jarmish war, and they are named among the slaving neighbours the Commonwealth thinks the Empire should focus on.
n.Grendel: The Grendel invasion of the Brass Coast destroyed the old embassy. The Commonwealth doubts it could stop the Grendel accepting Asavean help, and the trapped Lyceum magicians ask whether to prepare for another Grendel attack.
n.Highguard: The replacement Commonwealth embassy is being built at Hedra in Highguard's territory of Necropolis, and a Commonwealth siege engineer praised its land, progress and modern docks.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: their armies help illustrate the scale of the Jarmish war, and they are listed among the slaving neighbours the Empire is urged to fight.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly's call for captains to explore eastwards fed interest in a Sea of Steel expedition. The page also recalls Freeborn and Commonwealth soldiers fighting together at Siroc and the loss of the old embassy to the Grendel invasion.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the page names no Urizen people or deeds directly. Its link is through the Lyceum, whose Dean the Ambassador is asked to consult about the Commonwealth magicians sheltering behind its misty wards.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's detailed charting of the Bay is cited as something impossible to repeat across the vast Sea of Steel.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Commonwealth magicians trapped on the Lyceum isle ask whether Madruga is still in enemy hands.
t.Necropolis: Work on the new Commonwealth embassy is under way at Hedra, praised for its modern docks. Its closeness to Cargo and the Jarmish embassy raises concerns about rival ships sharing the Couros river.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is linked only through the Lyceum and the Commonwealth magicians sheltering there.

r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: The town of Hedra is the site of the new Commonwealth embassy, where engineer Poldi Hellebrant reported favourably on the land, the construction and the modern docks.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named directly; it is linked through the embassy works in Necropolis and concerns about Commonwealth and Jarmish ships sharing the Couros river.

Blood and mire.d: After the Druj invasion and the spilling of the Sephals Cauldron, roughly thirty thousand Imperial soldiers advanced, led by the Black Thorns. They were joined by twelve thousand Navarr-led warbands, a thousand Spears of the Pines and six thousand Knights of Glory serving Eleonaris. The Druj were cleared from the Lower Tarn Valley, which is now poisoned, and nine-tenths of the way out of Eastring. Nearly two thousand Imperial soldiers died in Eastring, which became haunted. The Towerjacks built temporary forts in Peakedge Song. A battle opportunity at Ashborder in Sweetglades offered a chance to stop two plans: a Siakha-empowered deluge that would flood East Ashes and destroy the Docks, and Cintra Blackstaff's ritual to rouse the vallorn.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun and the Gryphon's Pride marched from the Barrens to secure land and root out hidden Druj. Dawn's Knight-protector of Spring, Doctor Henri, was charged with stopping Druj ritualists from cursing the Barrens with storms.
n.Druj: The Druj brought in at least three more armies and fought a cautious, venomous campaign. Even so, they lost the Lower Tarn Valley and nearly all of Eastring, though they kept uncontested hold of East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks, where their ghulai prepared a 'cataclysm'.
n.Navarr: Navarr warbands formed the bulk of the twelve thousand who rallied to the Black Thorns to reclaim their homeland. Their steadings were left ruined, their dead haunt Eastring, and the vallorn now threatens to be woken against them.
n.Urizen: Druj ritualists threatened the Churnspire in Peregro. A flooded East Ashes would also cut army movement from Therunin into Morrow's Peregro and Zenith's Lustri.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and the Iron Helms marched from Ossium to aid their Navarr cousins, with Ser Gaspare's Knights of Glory fighting beside the Northern Eagle.

t.Morrow: The Towerjacks advanced through Morrow into Therunin, while the Shuddering Wrast moved into Peregro to destroy the Churnspire. If East Ashes floods, the route between Peregro and Therunin would be closed, leaving only Peakedge Song open.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Northern Eagle and Iron Helms marched into Therunin from Ossium, and veterans of the war in Ossium served among them.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Drainers, the Druj coven favoured by Siakha, were believed to hail from the far east of the Salt Flats.
t.Sarangrave: The invasion was launched from the marshes of Sarangrave, and the defeated Druj fell back through Eastring towards it. Cintra Blackstaff has strong ties to the Palace of the Sleepers there.
t.The Barrens: Two Dawnish armies and the Spears of the Pines marched south from the Barrens, and Hope's Rest was spared the cauldron's poison. Druj ritualists headed for the Swirling Cavern regio in the Untrod Groves to curse the territory with Thunderous Deluge.
t.Therunin: The Empire retook the Lower Tarn Valley and most of Eastring, leaving one poisoned and the other haunted, while the Druj kept East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks. Druj plans threatened to flood East Ashes and wake the vallorn, and Black Wind raiders were attacking Axou traders in the west.
t.Zenith: A flooded East Ashes would block army movement to Lustri. Any Druj trapped in Therunin might try to break south into Zenith's forests, and the Druj fear a repeat of their losses during the liberation of Zenith.

r.Morrow/Altis: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks pushed up through Altis on their way into Peakedge Song.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Shuddering Wrast advanced into Peregro to raze the Churnspire, and its Adjutor, Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard, was charged with stopping them. Flooding in East Ashes would cut Peregro off from Therunin for a year.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Sephals Cauldron's poison had been meant to taint the lake at Hope's Rest, but overturning it in the Tarn Valley left Hope's Rest safe for now.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes stayed under uncontested Druj control, ringed with walls of poison thorns, while ghulai gathered at the Feverwater Docks. An empowered Thunderous Deluge would make the region impassable for a year and sink the Docks.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring saw the most brutal fighting, amid Night-magic wards, and nearly two thousand Imperial soldiers died there. Druj control is almost broken, but the region is now haunted by Navarr and Druj dead.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Druj were driven out entirely, but the cauldron's spilled poison has left the valley poisoned, killing trees and fouling the waters.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Druj scouts reached its eastern steadings, and the Towerjacks raised temporary forts there, including a spiked palisade around Peakedge Stand. If Blackstaff wakes the vallorn, at least fifteen thousand vallornspawn could pour into the region.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The Druj pushed into the vallorn woods at Ashborder, where a battle opportunity offered the chance to stop the Blood Drainers' deluge and Cintra Blackstaff's ritual to rouse the vallorn. The ground is thick with vallorn miasma and Druj-driven giant insects.
r.Zenith/Lustri: If East Ashes floods, armies could no longer move between it and Lustri. Lustri's forests are also the only escape for Druj trapped in East Ashes.

Construct Bounders Hall of Meade.d: Following the Kith and Kin Wind of Fortune, Protectorate Thenrik, Legion Engineer, announced the construction of a Bounders Hall in Meade. It cost 12 white granite and 36 crowns and took three months to complete. The funding is credited in character to the houses of Talbot and Mudd of Mitwold. Matthias Talbot provided 12 wains of white granite and Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. With the hall complete, the senators of the Marches could appoint the Bailiff of Meade by unanimous vote for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE. Marcher beaters can now send their military units to defend Mitwold.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new national title, the Bailiff of Meade, appointed by unanimous vote of Marcher senators. Marcher beaters can now send their military units to defend Mitwold.

t.Mitwold: A Bounders Hall was built in Meade in Mitwold with backing credited to the local houses of Talbot and Mudd. It allows Marcher beaters' military units to defend the territory.

Construct Cascade of Living Flame.d: The Crystal Architect of the Spires, Tiberius Echostorm, announced the commission of a self-funded mana sinecure in Peregro, Morrow (named "Cascade of Living Fire" in the announcement), to produce mana crystals. It cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns and took three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 386YE, Rhode provided the 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. With the work complete, the position of Custodian of Living Flame can be appointed by unanimous vote of the senators of Urizen, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen's senators gain the power to appoint the new Custodian of Living Flame by unanimous vote, starting at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

t.Morrow: Morrow gains a new sinecure producing mana crystals, built with mithril and crowns supplied by Rhode.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro is the site of the newly completed Cascade of Living Flame, a mana-producing sinecure.

Construct Curstag's Way.d: Built under the We all stand Wind of Fortune, the highway honoured Curstag von Apulian Crimson Way. It was meant to support the unshackled orcs of Mareave and show its septs how the Empire builds up its people. As the Master of Rings announced it, some citizens of Apulian supported it. It cost 50 wains of white granite, 20 of mithril and 210 crowns, and took six months. Gancio di Catazar, League citizens, the Coalition of Stone and Struggle, Pathfinder Gaddak and others gave materials and money from Autumn 386YE to Summer 387YE. On completion it raised the investment level of Spiral businesses by one, worth 36 rings a season, and removed Icarion's under-developed quality.

n.Grendel: The highway runs into Mareave, which Grendel shared with the Imperial Orcs that season, and its completion removed the under-developed quality from Icarion there.
n.Imperial Orcs: The road was meant to support the unshackled orc cousins of Mareave and show its septs how the Empire builds up its people, and its completion developed Icarion in the territory the Imperial Orcs helped hold.
n.The League: A League undertaking announced by the Master of Rings in honour of a fallen League orc, it was built with League skill and gave Spiral's businesses a higher level of investment, worth 36 rings a season.
n.Urizen: The highway was to be built through Urizen vision and connects the Urizen territory of Redoubt to Spiral and Mareave.

t.Mareave: Mareave is the far end of the highway, and the finished road removed the under-developed quality from its region of Icarion.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt is one of the three territories the Grand Highway was built to connect, linking it to Spiral and Mareave.
t.Spiral: The great work was built in Spiral, and on completion it raised the level of investment in Spiral businesses by one, providing 36 rings a season.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the motion was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings.

r.Mareave/Icarion: The completion of Curstag's Way removed the under-developed quality from Icarion.

Construct Floerstrand.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hercynia, the motion passed with 15 thrones disbursed to the Senator for Sermersuaq. The sinecure required 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns and took three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer provided 7 thrones, 3 crowns and 20 wains of white granite, and Farren Silver Streams gave 1 crown. With Floerstrand complete, the position of Thane of Floerstrand was to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE, by unanimous vote of the senators of Wintermark.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new sinecure in its own lands, and its senators would choose the first Thane of Floerstrand by unanimous vote at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's senator proposed the motion and received the 15 thrones to build Floerstrand, a hot spring hall that grew out of the earlier appraisal of the territory's prosperity.

r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Tanikipari became the site of Floerstrand, a completed hot spring hall that is home to the new office of Thane of Floerstrand.

Construct Hartford Brewery.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Edmund Forster announced in Autumn 386YE that a sinecure called the Hartford Brewery would be built in Hartford in the Stock March region of Upwold. Its holder, the Hartford Brewmaster, would receive 16 wains each season and hold the post in tenure, appointed by the senators of the Marches. Construction required 16 white granite and 48 crowns and took three months. Forster provided 6 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 386YE and 16 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 386YE. With the brewery complete, the Brewmaster was due to be appointed for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

n.The Marches: The Marcher senators gained the right to appoint the Hartford Brewmaster in tenure, a post worth 16 wains a season, with the first appointment due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

t.Upwold: Upwold gained a new money-producing sinecure, the Hartford Brewery, built at Hartford with materials supplied by Edmund Forster.

r.Upwold/Stock March: The Hartford Brewery was built at Hartford in Stock March and was completed after the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Landskeeper's Study.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Redoubt, the motion took up the opportunity presented by the Thresher's Summer wind of fortune. The ministry cost 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour and was self-funded by prosperous Marcher citizens: John Fisher provided 4 thrones 3 crowns and 6 wains of white granite, Watkin 6 wains of white granite, and Farren Silver Streams 1 crown. Construction took three months. The Keeper of the Study is charged with spreading knowledge of the magical arts used to enchant farms, and is appointed annually by unanimous vote of the Marcher senators, first at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new national position, the Keeper of the Study, appointed each year by unanimous vote of its senators to spread knowledge of farm enchantment, with the building paid for by its own prosperous citizens.

t.Upwold: Upwold's senator proposed the motion, and the territory became home to the newly built Landskeeper's Study mana ministry.

r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The Landskeeper's Study was built at Oakwood in Ashbrook, making the region the seat of Marcher efforts to teach the magic of enchanting farms.

Construct Last Battle Wayhouse.d: Proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion followed the opportunity in the wind of fortune The way home. The wayhouse cost 18 wains of weirwood and 54 crowns and took three months to build, with materials and money given by Dax, Corwyn Heartsbane, Aneira Exiles End and others after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the new Keeper of the Last Battle title could be appointed annually by unanimous decision of the generals of Navarr, first at the Winter Solstice 386YE. Nesustak Forest and Turan Flats in Sarangrave gained the under threat quality. Navarri characters can now hold personal resources in the Barrens, and the Barrens' seasonal taxation rises by one throne.

n.Druj: The wayhouse was built expressly as a tool against the Druj, giving the Empire reconnaissance into their territory of Sarangrave and leaving two of its regions under threat.
n.Navarr: The generals of Navarr gain the right to appoint the Keeper of the Last Battle unanimously, and Navarri characters can now hold personal resources in the Barrens, benefiting from great works there.

t.Sarangrave: Druj-held Sarangrave is now watched from the new wayhouse across the border, and two of its regions have gained the under threat quality.

r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Nesustak Forest gained the under threat quality once the Last Battle Wayhouse was completed.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Turan Flats gained the under threat quality once the Last Battle Wayhouse was completed.

Construct Library of Worth.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Skarsind, the motion took up the opportunity in The Deer in the Sun wind of fortune. It was backed by the Imperial Orcs Assembly through a mandate enacted by Skywise Gralka. The folly cost 14 white granite and 42 crowns. Imperial Orc citizens supplied much of the white granite across several seasons, and individual donors such as Karrak, Ergot Di Cevia and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos gave crowns and stone. Once complete, the Library lets the Imperial Orcs, through the Weigher of Worth, add one word and its accompanying symbol to the collection each season.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc nation funded the Library with granite from its citizens, and through the Weigher of Worth it can now add one word and symbol to the collection each season to preserve its history.

t.Skarsind: The Library of Worth was raised in Guildenheim in Imperial Orc-held Skarsind, whose senator seconded the motion.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Gildermark is home to the new Library of Worth in Guildenheim, where the Imperial Orcs' collection of words and symbols is kept.

Construct Monument in Bastion.d: The monument was to be built in Sybella, in Sybella's Cross, to a design by Lady Josephine, with thanks to the generosity of Livia of the Spire of the Celestial Cascade. It required seven wains of white granite, one of mithril and 24 crowns, and would take three months to complete. Contributions came in from after the Autumn Equinox 386YE to after the Summer Solstice 387YE. Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum gave all seven wains of white granite and much of the money. Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave the mithril and several crowns, and smaller sums came from Rhys Nighthaven, Septus Sentinels Tower and Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard. Details of the finished monument were to be added to the Bastion page.

n.Highguard: The monument publicly honours Highborn and others who worked against discrimination toward lineaged people within Highguard, and Highborn including Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum gave much of the stone and money to build it.

t.Bastion: A folly to Lady Josephine's design was to be raised in Sybella, Sybella's Cross, with its granite and mithril supplied over the following seasons.

Construct Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Spiral, the motion commissioned the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy as a sinecure providing income to its holder. Construction required 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour (given as 3 thrones 6 crowns) and took three months. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the full materials and money after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the academy complete, the tenured title of Headmistress of the Open Fan Academy became available to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE, by unanimous vote of the senators of the League.

n.The League: The League gained a new tenured title, Headmistress of the Open Fan Academy, which its senators appoint by unanimous vote, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos became home to the Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy, a new money sinecure proposed by its own senator and completed with materials from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Open Fan Cicisbeo Academy was built in Cigno, taking three months and 10 wains of white granite to complete.

Construct Proud Quill Parcel.d: Announced in Autumn 386YE, the motion set out a herb sinecure to be planted in open land behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall in Hahnmark. The title attached to it would carry tenure and be appointed by unanimous agreement of the Wintermark senators. The listed cost was 16 wains of weirwood and 48 crowns, on top of standard costs, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Cormack Dun supplied 6 thrones and 16 wains of weirwood. Once construction was finished, the Guard of the Proud Quill Parcel became available for appointment by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators gain the power to appoint the Guard of the Proud Quill Parcel, a tenured herb-sinecure title, by unanimous decision from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark gains a new herb sinecure behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall, built with weirwood and coin provided by Cormack Dun.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: The Proud Quill Parcel is planted in open land behind the Proud Quill Ale Hall in Kalpamark, giving the region a completed herb sinecure.

Construct Statue of the White Bear.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, the folly was built under the Down the Cavalier Road wind of fortune at a cost of 30 white granite and 90 crowns, taking three months. Funding came in small donations after Autumn 386YE and Winter 387YE, then larger contributions of money and white granite after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice 387YE, notably from Dame Aurum De Castellan, Aenar de Forteair, Ser Gaheris Torawyr, Tallis Hart and Bertrand Gardener. On completion the Eastern Sky gained Cathan Canae's favour, allowing its general to issue the Embrace the Storm order once a year, a defensive order that limits movement but strengthens the army's defence of territory.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Eastern Sky army gained Cathan Canae's favour through the statue, letting its general once a year order it to embrace the storm, defending territory far more stubbornly at the cost of heavier casualties on both sides.

t.The Barrens: A statue of the White Bear was raised in the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn at Dawnguard in the Barrens, marking the site with a folly honouring Cathan Canae.

Glass and flame.d: After the Summer Solstice the Empire withdrew from Madruga. The Burning Falcon, Fire of the South, Red Wind Corsairs, Fist of the Mountains, Narwhal's Spear, Eastern Sky, Valiant Pegasus and Wolves of War invaded Feroz under cursed rains, probably raised by the Children of Wrecks. The Wolves' engines broke Oran within a day and Rahab's palace was razed. Bramar and Afar fell and slaves were freed. Gallum Fiersach still holds Mora's Rock. The pirates have seized the Cazar Straits. The Senate may now assign Feroz, which is ruined and under a ruinous rains curse. Surrendered Asavean priests await the Freeborn generals' judgement, and Grendel raiders are looting Sarvos's Isle of the Fox.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky, fighting beside the Summer war-witch Dindrayne and Eleonaris' trumpeters, kept pace with the Burning Falcon at the head of the invasion and pursued the fleeing Grendel through Fontargenta and Afarjasse.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj miasma is cited as an example of a fear effect that inspired Imperial soldiers might answer with anger.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Oran, Bramar, Afar and three regions of Feroz. Many of their fleeing ships were butchered by pirates, and their remaining forces hold Mora's Rock under Gallum Fiersach while their main army stays in Siroc Plains.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus under Zadok joined the overwhelming assault and wiped out Grendel fleeing towards the Suranni border before they could reach it.
n.The Brass Coast: All three Freeborn armies helped reclaim Feroz, and assigning the territory to the nation would restore its army supply. The Freeborn generals must also decide the fate of the surrendered Asavean priests in Oran.
n.The League: The Wolves of War and their Tassatan siege engineers broke Oran and fought the dock fire through the night. Meanwhile Grendel raiders are looting the Isle of the Fox, which supplies the Sarvos Mana Exchange.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains, alongside the Summer herald Elodian, and the Narwhal's Spear took Afar. They freed hundreds of slaves and executed the orcs who held them.

t.Bay of Catazar: Pirate vessels from the Cazar Straits fell on Grendel ships fleeing Oran across the bay, and only about one in three escaped.
t.Feroz: The Empire conquered Feroz and it awaits assignment by the Senate. The territory lies ruined after Rahab's rule and the fighting, and suffers a Spring curse of ruinous rains, while Mora's Rock remains in Grendel hands.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves' engineers hauled timber from Holberg's Misericorde forests, and a few Sand Fishers accompanied them.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Zadok recalls the Valiant Pegasus's hard-won victory in Kahraman, and the territory had given sanctuary to refugees from Feroz.
t.Kalino: An Iron Confederacy army camped just across the border watched as the Valiant Pegasus destroyed fleeing Grendel, amid rumours of a Suranni pact with the Grendel.
t.Madruga: The Imperial armies withdrew, leaving the Grendel and their Asaveans fortified in Siroc Plains. Foul weather persists, and the Spring-roused Scorrero has broken its banks into the Blightheart.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the strengthened Mora's Rock is compared to Reumah's Rest.
t.Sarvos: A company of Grendel is looting the Isle of the Fox's mana stockpiles, and Steward Wolfgang Wilheim Von Vanderghast must stop them or the Mana Exchange's supply will fall.
t.Segura: The Fire of the South moved through Segura under cover of darkness to strike Oranseri, and many displaced Ferozi had earlier found refuge in the territory.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The Fist of the Mountains and the Narwhal's Spear stormed Afar, Rahab's regional capital, and freed the slaves worked on his farms, bringing the region under Imperial control.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Children of Wrecks have seized the islands, which are now infested with beasts and pirates. The region has gained the island quality and cannot be attacked without naval support.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The Grendel made a stand at Bramar while pirates raided its docks, then fled before the Empire, and the region fell to Imperial forces.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Imperial advance faltered before Mora's Rock, which Gallum Fiersach holds with a large garrison and possibly the Wind Lord Saoirse. The region remains under Grendel control.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oran fell within a day to the Wolves of War's siege engines and Rahab's palace was reduced to rubble. The town was left heavily damaged by fighting and a dock fire.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: timber for the Wolves of War's siege engines was carted from the forests of Misericorde.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: Free Landing, stolen by the Children of Wrecks, is cited as the model for the pirates' seizure of the Cazar Straits.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: All eight Imperial armies and their Summer allies mustered at Cerevado in Lucksprings under Spring-infused rain before marching into Feroz.

Graveyard rats.d: After the Summer Solstice the Chamber of Commerce paid the Rat Kings a nine-month retainer, which may need renegotiating at the Spring Equinox 387YE. Their traps and dogs curbed the swarms, but Virtue's Respite, Empress Giselle's tomb, was attacked twice, halving its liao and money. Four people were eaten in grisly deaths, including the d'Hanuri brothers, and some citizens wondered whether the Silent Bell might investigate. The mountebank Brinton von Temeschwar, who claimed a token for parleying with the King of Rats, has vanished. Bishops preaching Vigilance or Loyalty gained congregants. Doctors proposed a Temeschwar Apothecary Supplies ministry for bladeroot and prismatic ink, and rumours spread of a great beast stalking the streets.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the d'Hanuri brothers' smashed bottle of wine had been brought all the way from Astolat.
n.The League: League citizens in Temeschwar gained respite from the swarms through the Rat Kings, whose contract may need renegotiating. Temeschwar congregations preaching Vigilance or Loyalty will gain two votes but lose a dose of liao, following Emil Radana von Temeschwar's statement in the League assembly.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the doctors blamed nearness to Varushka for some of the city's strange maladies and noted that bladeroot is easy to get from there, and one rumour blamed a Varushkan merchant's potion for a bravo's monstrous transformation.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a crude charm against the rats carried by one of the d'Hanuri brothers bore Wintermark runes.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: wine brought from Astolat appears in the story of the d'Hanuri brothers.
t.Temeschwar: The Rat Kings contained the plague in the city, but Giselle's Tomb produced half its usual income, four people were gnawed to death and rats still watched the streets. A proposed apothecary ministry in Hanari remained open until at least the end of the Spring Equinox 387YE.

Harvest of infamy.d: Three Asavean battleships, Leaping Bull, Wind Tamer and Venger's Blade, sailed through the Kongegőr and the Gullet into the newly dredged Westmere with about a dozen Asavean privateers and a dozen Grendel ships, aiming to burn Meade as Madruga had been ruined. After Imperial heroes slew Iacq Indurain in Madruga and seized his orders, the Drakes marched north. Nearly four thousand warband fighters and half the Forte Fidelis garrison joined them. The raiders were routed. Leaping Bull was trapped by merrow and scuttled, Venger's Blade fled badly damaged and Wind Tamer withdrew. Nearly a hundred Marcher soldiers died. Meanwhile High Voice Chiara led Asaveans and Grendel mercenaries towards the Phytwin Clearing in Kallavesa.

n.Grendel: Grendel ships sailed with the Asavean flotilla to plunder Meade and were beaten alongside their allies, while a Grendel mercenary company accompanied High Voice Chiara's attempt to desecrate the Phytwin Clearing.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Meade's walls were built against Jotun raiders, and Forte Fidelis kept watch on the border with Jotun-invaded Mournwold.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Leaping Bull and Wind Tamer were known for their attacks along the Brass Coast, and the raiders meant to do to Meade what had been done to Madruga and Siroc.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Tassato on their way north to Meade.
n.The Marches: The Drakes, warbands, the Forte Fidelis garrison and the people of Meade saved the Pride of the Marches from destruction, though nearly a hundred Marcher soldiers fell and the docks were damaged.
n.Wintermark: An Asavean priest and Grendel mercenaries threatened the Phytwin Clearing, a pilgrimage site tied to Gilda Ashwine, and the Speaker of the Crows, Ingrid, was charged with stopping them.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the slain Iacq Indurain is described as a liaison to Rahab, the late former Governor of Feroz.
t.Kallavesa: High Voice Chiara's force threatened to desecrate the Phytwin Clearing on the Pilgrim's Trail; if it was not stopped, the Trail would yield half the usual liao to Kallavesa's congregations for two seasons.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Iacq Indurain was slain and his orders seized in Madruga, and the Drakes marched north from there. The raiders hoped to repeat their earlier ruin of the territory.
t.Mitwold: The Asavean raid on Meade was defeated on its docks. Leaping Bull was sunk and Venger's Blade driven off, but nearly a hundred defenders were killed.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Forte Fidelis garrison could spare only half its strength because of the threat from Jotun-invaded Mournwold.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean ships were ordered to rendezvous at Caitun on the Sea of Snows before passing the Kongegőr, and some vessels trading with Caitun were destroyed as the fleet passed.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, though the flotilla's route ran through the Gullet towards the Westmere.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Tassato racing to reach Meade.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Upwold racing to reach Meade.

r.Mitwold/Meade March: Some townsfolk fled Meade into Meade March along the river-road to Wayford, while the Drakes and local defenders broke the raid on the town's harbour. The Marchers are already repairing the damaged docks.

Here to stay.d: Imperial Orcs, Golden Pyramid magicians and an Autumn enchantment aided Eilian, but the enchantment also helped resisters band together, raising the spectre of rebellion. He identified three groups: resentful former Grendel elites in Clisearn, cynical Eoradal orcs awaiting the Salt Lords' return, and the Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh. He proposed a Clisearn Grand Market great work with an Imperial Orc Steward of Works, and an adamant-infused fortified settlement at the Skouran ruins in Eoradal backed by the Tamazi. With the Illarawm mystagogue Bonesung Reller, he proposed protecting turtles to open talks with the Brine Turtles. He warned that using force would sour relations with all Broken Shore orcs. The Imperial Orcs sent Skywise Tylva to urge the Illarawm to negotiate.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Eilian studied past events in the Dawnish Barrens, and the Adamant Gate of Semmerholm served as the model for the proposed fortress.
n.Grendel: Former Grendel elites in Clisearn and orcs loyal to the Salt Lords in Eoradal resist the Empire in expectation of a Grendel return. Eilian warned that crushing them by force would strengthen Grendel resolve and help them raise and resupply armies.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were offered a Steward of Works position and a Tamazi-built fortified settlement in Mareave to cement their hold on the territory. Their assembly sent Skywise Tylva to urge the Illarawm to open peaceful negotiations with the Brine Turtles.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater, who carried out the appraisal, is Navarr.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League assembly urged its nation to offer expertise to help the Imperial Orcs in Mareave, as recounted elsewhere.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Eilian consulted the document Mareave and Urizen during his historical research.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Eilian considered past events in the Varushkan territory of Ossium as precedent.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: the Brine Turtles' warriors are fighting the Empire in Ayereed, and recent developments there highlighted the difficulty of moving water through Mareave.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Senate made it illegal for Imperial citizens to hunt turtles in the Bay, a gesture of respect for the Brine Turtles' sacred sea-turtles, at an estimated cost of no more than 4 thrones in taxes.
t.Mareave: Three southern regions remain uncooperative, which prevents the territory supporting an Imperial army. The Senate's recognition of the orcs there as foreigners opened the way to proposed great works and negotiations.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Eilian examined how matters went in Ossium when considering how to make peace with conquered peoples.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the adamant-infused Adamant Gate in Semmerholm was cited as the model for the proposed Eoradal fortress.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Eilian recovered from the effects of Spiral, and the Eoradal orcs compare the Empire's hold on Mareave to the Grendel's temporary conquests of Spiral.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Eilian looked at events in the Barrens for lessons in reconciling with conquered people.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: Eilian consulted scholars in the independent city, whose people already hold foreigner status, a privilege the Clisearn orcs resent.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Resentful former Grendel families led by Devan Adahr, Savurn Marr and Regan Tholdie resist the Empire. A proposed Clisearn Grand Market at Ohwinn Dell, with an Imperial Orc Steward of Works, could remove the region's uncooperative quality now that its orcs are foreigners.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Uthni and other cynical orcs expect the Grendel to return. Eilian and Ketus Stonewalk proposed an adamant-infused fortified settlement at the Skouran ruins to prove the Imperial Orcs are here to stay.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The proud, frightened Brine Turtles sept, centred on Fioroult, resists the Empire while its warriors fight under Grendel banners. The turtle-hunting ban and Illarawm diplomacy are meant to open negotiations with its elders.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Mentioned in passing: the people of Sinfoyard had already been granted foreigner status under the treaty with former Salt Lord Ehsan.

Hey now how you doing?.d: Kimus found Emperor Frederick's Pauper's Key and sent a report to Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo. Sadogua offered to keep the Lyceum's warding mists up until Winter 387YE if asked through a Declaration of Alignment, and offered to make magic items for Navarr magicians. Ephisis's herald Keel publicly sought Flavio i Flav i Riqueza to escort him to his vault. Lashonar abandoned Summoning the Loquacious Birds and priority Caucus Forum access. Sung extended her riddle about a herald's name. Irra Harah offered to enchant small tokens of personal struggle. Zakalwe ended the Pearls of Manush after one was used against the Grendel. A thousand of Tharim's knights stayed near Quzar. Skirmishes were called against the Feasters of Marrow in Holberg and the Speakers of Famine in Astolat.

n.Dawn: Dawnish citizens, especially those who had backed killing the Montanians or oppressing orcs, received Lashonar's unsettling vision. Dawn's Astolat became the last refuge of the Speakers of Famine.
n.Druj: The Pearls of Manush, given only for the war against the Druj, were withdrawn after misuse. Lashonar chose not to send the commissioned vision to orcs suffering in Druj lands.
n.Grendel: A Pearl of Manush used on armies fighting the Grendel in Mareave broke the deal with Zakalwe. The threat of Grendel raids on the Lyceum drove Sadogua's offer to extend its wards.
n.Navarr: Sadogua offered to turn materials sent by Navarr magicians and covens into magic items by the Winter Solstice, as a smaller boon ahead of their war with the vallorn.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn figures were at the centre of several offers: Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo was to receive Kimus's report and Flavio i Flav i Riqueza was sought by Ephisis's herald. Madruga's Lyceum and the town of Quzar faced magical concerns.
n.The League: A League Assembly mandate in Holberg left only the Feasters of Marrow to confront. The Speakers of Famine hunted by Vigilance had come from Temeschwar, and Spiral was cited in the Conclave's removal of Lashonar's amity.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Ematius of Urizen, as Archmage of Winter, had declined Tharim's new offer, and Sadogua's earlier item-making for the Urizen is cited as precedent.
n.Varushka: Varushkans, notably those who had called for suppressing the Rahvin or terrorising the Black Wind, received Lashonar's vision of a rebuilt Ossium. Irra Harah's heralds were to return enchanted items at the Varushkan Hearth Fire.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Irra Harah's agents were to return enchanted items at the Tree of Names in Wintermark.

t.Astolat: The Speakers of Famine, a dozen boon-bearing followers of Agramant, were cornered at their last refuge here. Jared of the Silent Tower was responsible for killing them before they could flee deeper into the Empire.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South left Madruga to fight the Grendel here, and the Children of Wrecks' hold on its Cazar Straits fed Sadogua's concern for the Lyceum.
t.Holberg: The Feasters of Marrow, the last cannibal cult left in Holberg, planned a profane ritual in the Wunderkind Woods. Kanute Adelaar van Holberg was responsible for killing them.
t.Madruga: Sadogua offered to keep the hidden Lyceum's wards up for another year against the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks. A thousand of Tharim's Ashen Knights remained camped near Quzar.
t.Mareave: During the Winter Solstice, two armies enchanted with a Pearl of Manush fought the Grendel here, which ended Zakalwe's supply of Pearls to Highwatch.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar's vision showed Ossium rebuilt from ruin into one of the Empire's most prosperous territories.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: recent events here are among those that angered Lashonar.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Conclave's declaration removing Lashonar's amity claimed the eternal had endangered the citizens of Spiral.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Speakers of Famine originated here before fleeing to Astolat.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Lashonar was known to favour peace in the Barrens and was angered by recent events there.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: these islands next to the Lyceum isle, held by the Children of Wrecks, are cited as a threat behind Sadogua's offer to keep the wards up.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: A thousand of Tharim's Ashen Knights stayed camped in Lightsea near Quzar after the Fire of the South left, worrying the townsfolk, who want them moved or the threat explained.

Houses of Silence.d: Under the Vandersaar family the Alivetti estates have become a rich enclave outside Imperial law, where the illegal Ocean's Caress is sold and eternals declared enemies of the Empire may be approached. Magistrates have arrested citizens bringing the drug home, foiled a smuggling attempt into Riposi, and heard rumours of Sarcophan interest in interdicted Druj potions. The Bladgoud Tuiniers offered discounted narcotics to the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce in return for endorsing their handelsschool, at the cost of income from the College of the Liberated; the Chamber declined. Separately, the Community of Silence sought 40 wains of white granite at 4 thrones each, and Imperial artists, for a Silent Manse temple. The Vigilance assembly warned of heresy, and the Synod could delay the work through judgements.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the interdicted potions Warming Armour and Weakening Sun, which Sarcophan merchants are rumoured to want, originated with the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the curse storms Imperial magicians raised in the conflict with the Grendel had aggrieved the Vandersaar, prompting an apology from the Ambassador.
n.The League: The League's Sarvosan business owners were offered Sarcophan narcotics in exchange for endorsing a rival merchant school, and chose to decline. A League national assembly mandate was identified as a way to delay the heretical temple by three months.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Delves had once proposed establishing a trading enclave in Varushka, before the Senate chose the Alivetti estates instead.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the threat of the Children of Wrecks had raised the cost of shipping white granite for the temple to the Bay of Catazar.
t.Sarvos: The Sarcophan enclave on the old Alivetti estates in Sarvos sold drugs illegal in the Empire, leading to arrests at the border. The city's Chamber of Commerce rejected the handelsschool deal, keeping its full College of the Liberated income, while a Sarcophan temple began rising in the enclave.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Kraken's Ink was renamed Stoneheart Syrup to avoid confusion with the real kraken's ink brought back by hunters on the Sea of Snow.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: in a play described in the fiction, the drug-supplying cicisbeo is first said to be from Temeschwar before being revealed as Sarcophan.

r.Sarvos/Riposi: A band of smugglers tried to bring a significant quantity of Ocean's Caress into Riposi hidden in barrels of salt fish, but were stopped thanks to an anonymous tip-off.

How to be dead.d: Hundreds of Rod and Shield battlemages, supplied from Hahnmark, Miaren and Upwold, descended into the sinkhole. Every member fell sick, and the fallen rose again as husks, as at Isember. The expedition rescued lost miners in a vast cavern, but hidden worshippers struck and over a hundred died. Survivors revealed that cultists had fled into Goldglades and the Crimson Band were camped in Wood Heath. The Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield is to kill the followers, and the Imperial Huntsmarshall the Crimson Band. The Delver of the Depths is to use Alexi Isembrioch's skull, sent by the Fellowship of the Black Goose, to lure out and kill the Braying Lord in Vardstein Vale.

n.Dawn: Knights of Dawn fought alongside the Rod and Shield's battlemages in the push downward, and nine Dawnish heroes are named among those who explored the depths.
n.Navarr: The Braying Lord's worshippers fled south into Navarr's Goldglades, threatening to reach the Blood Red Roads of Miaren and spread the plaguewulf's taint; four Navarr heroes explored the depths.
n.The League: The plaguewulf's lair threatens Temeschwar, and the Delver of the Depths is asked to lure out and kill the Braying Lord in Vardstein Vale; two League heroes are named among the explorers.
n.The Marches: Upwold supplied the expedition as a territory bordering the sinkhole, and five Marcher heroes are named among those who explored the depths.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly unanimously urged Varushkans to aid the Rod and Shield, inspiring the Fellowship of the Black Goose to send the skull of the former Boyar of Isember to help destroy the Braying Lord.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark heroes fought in the depths, and the Crimson Band camped in Wood Heath threaten to find sanctuary in Hahnmark and spread the plaguewulf's taint into Wintermark, possibly giving rise to a horror like the Deadwood Knight.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark supplied the expedition, and the Crimson Band are now camped in its Wood Heath, threatening to vanish into its wilds unless the Imperial Huntsmarshall destroys them.
t.Karsk: The Fellowship of the Black Goose, guardians of the ruins of Isember in Karsk, provided the skull of Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch from their ossuary to help lure out the Braying Lord.
t.Miaren: Miaren supplied the expedition, and the plaguewulf's followers are encamped in Miaren, seeking to reach its roads and spread the sickness across the Empire.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: a Varushkan warden in the opening fiction remarks that the threatened lands are far from Miekarova and the Razors.
t.Temeschwar: The Braying Lord has nested in the sinkhole threatening Temeschwar, and the Delver of the Depths is asked to lure it out and kill it in Temeschwar's Vardstein Vale.
t.Upwold: Upwold, bordering the sinkhole, supplied the Rod and Shield expedition and is named among the territories threatened by the plaguewulf.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: The Crimson Band mercenaries, who struck a bargain with the Braying Lord, have made camp in Wood Heath and can be attacked there through the Sentinel Gate by the Imperial Huntsmarshall.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: The Braying Lord's worshippers fled south into Goldglades, where the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield is asked to kill them before they reach the roads.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Vardstein Vale is where the Braying Lord first entered the sinkhole, and where the Delver of the Depths is asked to use the skull to lure it out and destroy it.

Hyenas and herbs.d: The Asavean bounty on ships trading with the Empire has cut Sarcophan visits, so Imperial fleets trading with the Delves earn better profits. The Delves want to know the Empire's plan against the Children of Wrecks. The Vandersaar offered eight more wains of white granite a season at the Concordium Docks. The Debruin family offered weirwood if the Pallas Docks in Cargo were reopened. The House of the Hyena would invest in the Brass Coast once the pirates are dealt with. The Kruidenkenner refused to cut herb prices but proposed specific herbs for Sybella and a larger Meade magazijn. Jasmijn Dijkgraaf offered to carry a letter to the Elakar for eleven thrones. Hahnmark's farmers accepted, giving up Brenna's Gift income for viezesmaak.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Delves' treaties with the Grendel do not protect their ships from the Children of Wrecks, and the Grendel are named as Asavean allies in burning Siroc.
n.Highguard: The Kruidenkenner proposed that the High Herbalist of Sybella receive set amounts of true vervain and marrowort instead of random herbs, to be arranged through the Ambassador. Their Crown's Quay magazijn remains their largest Imperial investment.
n.The Brass Coast: The House of the Hyena, prompted by Damian i Martan i Erigo, wants to sell mithril and artisan metals to Freeborn markets and settle at Calvos or Quzar. Allied families would pay well to salvage drowned Siroc, but none of this will happen until the Children of Wrecks are dealt with.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner sell herbs to the Clearing House in Tassato, and the Sarcophan enclave in Sarvos is covered in a separate wind.
n.The Marches: The Kruidenkenner offered to expand their magazijn in Meade so the Master of the Root and Stem could buy two more specific herbs. The offer went untaken at the Equinox but stays open until the end of Winter 386YE.
n.Urizen: The Debruin family offered up to 15 wains of weirwood a season if the Pallas Docks in Cargo were refitted as the Debruin Docks. The same motion could make the Prime Factor title an Urizen national position. No one took up the offer at the Equinox.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Kruidenkenner merchants use the Sarcophan mooring in Ivarsgard to trade with Varushkan herbalists, though demand there has fallen sharply.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark's farm owners voted to grow vlinderbloem for the Kraft brothers, giving up Brenna's Gift income in exchange for viezesmaak. Wintermark's Thanmir Hrafnar is the only person from whom Jasmijn Dijkgraaf will accept an Elakar letter.

t.Bastion: The High Herbalist of Sybella may switch the Kruidenkenner herb supply for the Anvil hospital to set amounts of true vervain and marrowort, at the same price as before.
t.Bay of Catazar: Attacks by the Children of Wrecks across the Bay are forcing Sarcophan captains to hire more marines and ships. The Delves expect the Empire to deal with the pirates.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's farmers voted to give land over to vlinderbloem. Each farmer now receives two doses of viezesmaak a season, and Brenna's Gift income is lost while the scheme lasts.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Kraft brothers plan to export viezesmaak through the revitalised port of Fisk along the new route to Faraden.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner trade with Varushkan herbalists at the Sarcophan mooring in Ivarsgard, though demand there has declined sharply.
t.Madruga: Sarcophan families would pay the treasury or Madruga's senator well for exclusive rights to salvage drowned Siroc, but only once the Children of Wrecks are dealt with.
t.Mitwold: An offered expansion of the Kruidenkenner magazijn in Meade, costing 8 weirwood and 24 crowns, would add two herb tracks for the Master of the Root and Stem. It remains open until the end of Winter 386YE.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay is named as the association's largest and best-known Imperial investment.
t.Redoubt: A 90-crown refit could reopen the Pallas Docks in Cargo as the Debruin Docks, with a bear statue, and bring up to 15 wains of weirwood a season. The offer was not taken up at the Equinox.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti Estates is covered in another wind, and a sailor recalls buying an enchanted carving there.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Kruidenkenner merchants regularly sell herbs to the Clearing House in Tassato.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the threat of Dho'uala has made the Semmerlak less appealing to the Kruidenkenner.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: the page names the port of Fisk as the Krafts' export route to Faraden, without saying where it lies.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Hyena interest in Madruga's coast, including salvage of Siroc and a possible presence at Calvos or Quzar, waits on the Empire dealing with the Children of Wrecks. The page does not say which of these sites lie in Lightsea.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: the page names the Kruidenkenner Magazijn at Crown's Quay as their main Imperial investment, without saying where it lies.

Irreconcilable differences.d: The law would have banned preaching the Way anywhere in the Archipelago and criminalised helping others to do so. That put it in open conflict with Synod mandates. Aspar's mandate created the Anchor the Way commission, the Freeborn enabled smuggling missionaries to Asavea, and Lutobor Branislavovich Glinka urged citizens to double down on Asavea. Amika Acciai was also recognised as an exemplar. The Plenum sees the Way as an existential threat and has increased aid to the Grendel. A successful veto would stoke Asavean fury, while a failed one would doom the sects. The Sevenfold Path also sought virtuous magicians, including the Cerularios. Shardbearer later said the Senate would respect the veto.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo angrily warns Othet not to lecture her about the Druj during their argument.
n.Grendel: The Grendel are the Plenum's proxies in its war on the Empire, already bolstered with Asavean warships, and they could expect still more Asavean support if the missionaries continued.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Dagon of Highguard, former Champion of Loyalty, carried the Loyalty Assembly's mandate, and earlier Synod mandates had urged Highborn wayfarers to preach the Way abroad.
n.The Brass Coast: Pacheco i Shartha i Guerra's mandate set Freeborn captains to smuggling missionaries and aid into Asavea, and Freeborn corsairs carried the Sevenfold Path magicians there. All of this would have been lost had the ban come into force.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's surprise attack on Meade is cited as evidence of Asavea's escalating hostility.
n.Urizen: Glinka's mandate did not reach a greater majority, so it had no particular impact in Urizen, unlike most other nations, whose national assemblies drew extra attention on the issue.
n.Varushka: Lutobor Branislavovich Glinka, a Varushkan, enacted the General Assembly mandate to double down on Asavea. Paradoxically, it had no particular impact in Varushka itself.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, raised the contentious ban. After the Synod's veto, Shardbearer declared that the Senate would respect the decision.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo describes the Grendel as battered in Ayereed.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's attack on Meade is described as striking the far side of the Empire from the Bay of Catazar.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were rousted from Feroz.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator, Rane Shardbearer, raised the motion banning preaching in Asavea and later acknowledged the Synod's veto in the Senate.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were beaten back in Madruga.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Hamelo says the Grendel were rousted from Mareave, and the loose lips of Beoraidh mercenaries revealed Catella Cerularios's interest in Glistering.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Plenum's surprise attack on Meade is cited as part of Asavea's escalating campaign against the Empire.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: loose-lipped Beoraidh mercenaries are the reason the Empire learned of Catella Cerularios's interest in the relic Glistering.

Nightcall.d: The mystics of Ishal have left their aviary to travel Wintermark seeking omens. Asked by the Raven Seer to find alternatives to Dripping Echoes of the Fen, Wyr proposed three fanes, each costing 10 mithril, 10 ilium and 30 crowns: the Dreaming Barrow for Feather on the Breeze, the Toadstone for the Toad King, and a converted Aviary at Ishal for the Speaker in Dreams. The omens say that all three together would anchor the Night realm around Kallavesa and make it much harder to invade. Brennir Calversbairn also called in a favour to arrange a meeting for up to nine Wintermark magicians, chosen by the Shaman, with Sadogua at the Equinox. The mystics offered further proposals for the coming year.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are cited as foes that Sadogua has little reason to like and that Lashonar would not welcome, and Ephisis's protection of an apparent fane in Jotun lands is given as a precedent.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the patronage that Spiral Dancer gives the magicians of the Deathless Cave in Spiral is cited as an example of a fane drawing an eternal into defending a region.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the mystics point to Urizen studies of magical resonance to explain why three fanes together might have a potent and unexpected effect.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's mystics offered the nation three fane commissions to defend Kallavesa, each with a Wintermark steward, and a chance for up to nine of its magicians to bargain with Sadogua over his withdrawn favour. They also offered to bring further proposals for the coming year in answer to problems the Ravenseer sends them by ritual.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa is the territory the proposals aim to protect. The mystics believe that three night fanes placed around its borders would shroud the marshes and help defend them against invasion from any quarter.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is cited as a precedent, where Spiral Dancer's patronage of the Deathless Cave's magicians appears to give the eternal a stake in the region's safety.

r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: Feather on the Breeze has suggested a fane at the Dreaming Barrow in Rundhal Marsh, an ancient mound where sleepers have prophetic dreams. She would likely take a personal interest in protecting the site.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Wyr proposed a fane housing the Toadstone, an onyx carving near Westerhal in West Marsh, to be ceded to the Toad King. The local wizards would become a fraternity supporting it.

Rebels and loyalists.d: The Pride Assembly upheld recognition of Esme Hooper, Mary Digger, Ezekial Boon, Henry Killinghall, Maggie John and Tom John, together, as ringleaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion; the General Assembly must now decide. Passing it may look like the Synod siding with the miners, and rejecting it like siding with the farmers, though either is manageable. A true liao memorial, sought by Jedediah Boon and his allies, would reopen the question of who appoints Marcher senators. Separately, the Marcher Assembly revoked Hal Talbot 108-16. The Loyalty Assembly must act at the Winter Solstice: denouncing the revocation risks conflict between assemblies, while failing to do so loses the Eyes of Loyalty.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: any rebel memorial is presumed to be built in Ore Hills once the Jotun there are dealt with.
n.The Marches: Marchers face renewed tension between miners and yeofolk over the rebels' recognition, and a possible split as some Loyal dedicates question their own national assembly's revocation of Hal Talbot.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator Hal Talbot was revoked by the Marcher Assembly for showing loyalty to his house over his nation, a judgement the Loyalty Assembly may denounce at the Winter Solstice.
t.Mournwold: The old rift between the miners of the central and southern Mourn and the northern yeofolk is stirred again, and a consecrated memorial to the rebels would strengthen independent spirit and revive disputes over who appoints the Mournwold senator.

r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The region that gave the rebellion its name is the presumed site of a proposed true liao memorial to its leaders, should recognition and a writ of consecration both pass once the Jotun are dealt with.

Rising in Runegrott.d: The Rising Tide found that the artisans near Isenbrad's shrine in Runegrott could produce far more if they had more orichalcum and ambergelt. Each offer was made to a specific title for a year: Bloodcloaks to the Grimnir of Wittal Grove, mage armours to the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield, Pauper's Keys to the Guardian of Afal and Lodestone Shears to the Seer of the Spiral Sword. A Cowl of Ashes would go to whoever the Benefactor of Regalia named. If enough items were bought, the Keeper of the Runegrott might gain a temporary ministry trading materials for coin. Separately, Elik and Savra of the Great Forest Orcs were to meet five Wintermarkers chosen by the Raven Seer.

n.Navarr: Navarri members of the Rising Tide, Gethyn and Rayna Swiftongue, led the effort. The Senator for Hercynia, the former Senator for Therunin and the Inquisitor of Loyalty were asked to mediate a meeting with Great Forest Orcs at the heart of the Navarr camp.
n.The League: The Seer of the Spiral Sword was offered one or two Lodestone Shears for ambergelt, which Gethyn hoped would bring the Empire's runeforge keepers closer together.
n.Wintermark: The artisans of Runegrott stood to gain the resources they lacked, and the Keeper of the Runegrott might later win a temporary trading opportunity. The Raven Seer was asked to choose five representatives to talk weirwood and the defence of the Kallavesi swamps with Great Forest Orcs.

t.Spiral: The Seer of the Spiral Sword was given the option to trade ambergelt for Lodestone Shears made by the Runegrott artisans.

Seven locks.d: A herald apparently of the Whisper Gallery invited the Archmage of Night and cadets investigating the Tomb of Achism to meet the Veiled Caballero. Kaela invited named groups to offer songs of death and proposed recruiting dying heroes into her Grim Legion. Basileia Brazen of the City of Locks offered knowledge for tempest jade. Adamant declined parley but offered to help build an unbreakable fortification in Segura. The Centipede General declined parley and pressed the Navarr to build it a fane. Roshanwe invited covens to discuss Combing the Beach. Azoth prepared a brew to realign the Terunael Singing Stone. Afterwards the Conclave paid tempest jade for intelligence on the Grendel's Salt Lords.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Adamant compared his promised Segura fortification to the unbreakable Gate in Semmerholm.
n.Druj: The Centipede General said it had already withdrawn some support from the Druj and would not favour either side in Therunin, though it would not stop them using rituals drawing on its aid. Arhallogen keeps offering his protective magics to the orcs while refusing them to the Empire.
n.Grendel: Basileia Brazen offered knowledge to help the Empire in its war with the Grendel. After a Conclave declaration of Concord, tempest jade was paid for insight into Grendel society and the Salt Lords who rule it.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's herald came as a Highborn cataphract bearing the banner of a long-dead chapter, and she disclaimed any interest in enforcing a claim to Rhonwen's Fall.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Veiled Caballero wanted cadets who had investigated the Tomb of Achism, particularly its connection to the Jotun and a missing archivist.
n.Navarr: Kaela is sending her herald Marcescence to help against the Folly of Terunael. The Centipede General will renew its boons once the Navarr build it a fane. Azoth, delighted by their acceptance of the Great Forest Orcs as kin, prepared a brew to realign the Terunael Singing Stone to the Navarr, though they must guard it from theft.
n.The Brass Coast: Adamant offered the Master of the Koboldi an unbreakable rank-two fortification in Segura, built in a year, if commissioned by Summer 388YE. Azoth took a keen interest in what the river's rise had wrought in Madruga.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Archmages of Winter and Spring are both of Urizen, and Adamant declined to discuss the Eye of Morrow.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi left Anvil for Karov to help put the final touches to the Great Hall of Fabric Arts.
n.Wintermark: Eliina Lailasdottir of Wintermark, Archmage of Night, received two answers: the Whisper Gallery meeting and Azoth's gift. Azoth told her it could not help close the destructive regio in Hahnmark.

t.Hahnmark: Azoth said nothing could survive the light of the destructive regio in Hahnmark long enough to close it. It suggested gathering residues from other Cold Sun-tainted places and sending another plenipotentiary.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's koboldi headed to Karov to help finish the Great Hall of Fabric Arts.
t.Madruga: Azoth was excited by what the mix of magic, water and star-metal had created in Madruga after the river's rise. It noted that the conflux of Winter, Spring and Night there mirrors the Ring of Adversity.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named, but the Navarr campaign against the Folly of Terunael drew offers of help from Kaela's herald Marcescence and the Centipede General.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Adamant declined to speak of the Eye of Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Kaela said she makes no claim she means to enforce on Rhonwen's Fall and advised letting it collapse into ruin.
t.Segura: Adamant offered that a fortification commissioned in Segura by the Master of the Koboldi could be built as a rank-two, unbreakable stronghold within a year, with its foundations infused with adamant. The offer is open until Summer 388YE, given the rising river, and can be invoked only once.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the unbreakable Gate in Semmerholm was cited as the model for Adamant's promised fortification.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Roshanwe's herald came dressed in the garb of a Suaq hunter.
t.Therunin: The Centipede General acknowledged the Druj had made a good showing in Therunin but said it was not inclined to favour either side in the fighting there.

Signal fire.d: Rane, who raised the Senate motion criminalising preaching in Asavea, spoke on the Emperor's behalf, saying Vesna would accept the Empire's choice and that missionaries could not be faulted in Virtue. She warned that Asavea would respond, that wars were at a knife-edge, and that losing sixty thrones a season in trade would cost more than feeding an army. She asked whether priests would sacrifice the Brass Coast, the Marches, Therunin or the Holy City, and demanded they either support the Empire's defences or stay their hand. The Synod upheld the veto; Rane then made a Senate statement, endorsed by the Senate, respecting the Synod's decision.

n.Navarr: Rane cited Navarr's declaration that it was time to fulfil its oldest oath and take the fight to the vallorn, asking whether missionaries would risk sacrificing that campaign.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark senator, Rane spoke for the Throne, recalling how she had brought Pride to Kallavesa to bolster Wintermark in its hour of need.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator delivered the address, citing her efforts in its swamps as proof of her willingness to pay a price, and later made the Senate statement accepting the Synod's veto.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: named among the lands, alongside the Brass Coast, the Marches and the Holy City, that could pay the price if Asavea retaliated against Imperial missionaries.

Steel and salt.d: Joined by around a thousand soldiers under independent captains, the three armies entered the Cravanclosh, a forest turned to stone where choking ash, wound-petrifying infection and scarce water hampered them. They collided with the Hamsin and Brine Turtles, who had been marching north to attack Mareave. Commander Marradhol, granddaughter of Salt Lord Azshur, arrived with nearly ten thousand reinforcements and took command, causing friction with the Hamsin. The cautious Grendel lost more troops than the Empire and were pushed slowly south. Highborn scouts found petrified ambergelt and identified two fortifications, Stormlords Rise and Beynagahoyne. Uncooperative Mareave septs raised army upkeep by three tenths. Lord Alessia Heraclien was found carrying money to fund mercenaries at Stormlords Rise.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: The Barrens is named as one of the lands the Golden Axe helped bring into the Empire.
n.Grendel: The Hamsin's planned attack on Mareave was thwarted, and Commander Marradhol's forces took over the defence of Ayereed. The Grendel suffered heavier casualties as they were driven slowly south through the Petrified Forest.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun marched into Ayereed to claim new land, using supernatural strategic insight to counter the Grendel and exploit friction between Marradhol and the Hamsin. However, Brine Turtle septs in their newly secured Mareave remained resentful and uncooperative.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe led the advance and drove the Grendel back most aggressively, coping best with the hostile forest. Their soldiers discovered that the giant scorpions were edible and excelled at preserving and seizing water.

t.Ayereed: Imperial armies invaded this largely unknown Grendel territory, came almost halfway to conquering the Petrified Forest and learned of two fortifications, Stormlords Rise and Beynagahoyne. Ayereed is also too arid for the Rivers of Life and Rivers Run Red rituals to work as expected.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: a Senate-backed survey five years earlier mapped the Bay's coastline but revealed little of Ayereed's interior.
t.Mareave: Mareave served as the staging ground for the invasion of Ayereed, but its septs' control of scarce fresh water made supplying the armies hard and increased their upkeep. The Hamsin had been marching to attack it before being intercepted.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a land the Golden Axe helped bring under the Imperial banner.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as a land the Golden Axe helped bring into the Empire.

r.Ayereed/Cornaghan: Lord Alessia Heraclien and Grendel guards were tracked through Cornaghan carrying a chest of at least twenty thrones to hire mercenaries for Stormlords Rise. The General of the Seventh Wave was given the task of stopping them.
r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: The Grendel city of Gainmeachdubh is the seat of Salt Lord Azshur, whose household troops under Commander Marradhol formed the bulk of the reinforcements that took charge of Ayereed's defence.
r.Ayereed/Petrified Forest: The Cravanclosh became the battleground, where ash, petrifying infection, scarce water and giant scorpions troubled the armies. The Empire pushed the Grendel south and was almost halfway to conquering the region, and scouts found petrified ambergelt in abandoned logging camps.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn was one of three Mareave regions disinclined to support Imperial troops, which added to the upkeep burden on the armies in Ayereed.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal was one of three Mareave regions disinclined to support Imperial troops, which made supplying the invasion of Ayereed harder and costlier.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Brine Turtle sept watched the armies with fearful, resentful suspicion and offered no welcome in Fioroult. Their warriors fighting for the Grendel tried in vain to slip scouts through Imperial lines to reach their septmates there.

The Synod speaks.d: Gaelen Embercast's Assembly of Nine statement (7-1) declared the vallorn the greatest spiritual threat and urged every nation to join the war. Statements from Kaspar Yakovitch von Holberg (League, 288-48) and Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti (Varushka, 222-10) recalled debts owed to the Navarr. Each nation could enact one of three competing mandates that would shape later opportunities to aid the Navarr, but would also stop other national calls to action having effect for a year. Dawn, Highguard and Urizen passed conflicting statements, none by greater majority. Other nations had only this season to respond. The Varushkan Wisdom mandate and the League Ambition mandate were enacted, and Highguard sent Hazelelponi to call the grey pilgrims home.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Assembly passed both supportive and cautionary statements, none with a greater majority. The nation could still take a clear stand this season.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page touches them only through links to vallorn-related places such as Sarangrave.
n.Highguard: Highguard was praised for standing with the Navarr but passed mixed statements. It later enacted a mandate sending Hazelelponi to call the grey pilgrims home to prepare for war with the vallorn.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; only earlier Liathaven vallorn events appear in the further reading.
n.Navarr: The Navarr gained the backing of the Assembly of Nine, the League and Varushka for their war against the vallorn, with two-thirds of stridings already leaving the trods to prepare.
n.The League: The League Assembly could commit its citizens to aiding the Navarr through its wealth, senators and engineering skills. It enacted the Ambition mandate, sending Ortenzia di Sarvos to urge new ways to fight the vallorn, which barred other national calls to action for a year.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Assembly passed conflicting statements both supporting the Navarr and urging delay, none with a greater majority. The nation could still take a clear stand this season.
n.Varushka: Varushka, with three armies, mithril and artisan resources, could commit to aiding its Navarr cousins. It enacted the Wisdom mandate, empowering Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti, and its people will not answer other national calls to action for a year.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande appears only in further reading links to earlier vallorn adventures and rituals.
t.Hercynia: The page raised the possibility that Varushkan artisan resources could help the Navarr raise their new army in Hercynia.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan statement recalled that the Navarr stood with Varushka when Karsk was attacked.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in further reading links to earlier fighting against its vallorn.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named on the page and is connected only as Navarr land.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave appears only in a further reading link to an expedition to Bendol.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: Bendol appears only in a link to the earlier report of the expedition Into Béantal Dol.
