The fayre fight.d: Lady Griffonsbane invited the sixteen people who had fought in every stage of the Grand Tour to a series of one-on-one bouts at Anvil. The prize was a magical weapon made by the Moon Weavers of the Semmerstones. The Reeve, Trystan Tanner, organised a fayre around the contest, open to all. The Culwich Weavers gave a Watchers' Flute to Emmeline Weaver for 'Race for the Barrens'. The Hidden Prince offered the Twisted Torc, which brings one season of prosperity to a territory, to the new Knight-protector of Autumn. Bedegrayne of the Silver Nightingales asked the Senate to clarify the Challenger in Waiting. The Senate removed its tourney and made it an Assembly appointment.

n.Dawn: Dawn's nobles and yeofolk celebrated the Barrens conquest with tourneys and a fayre, and Rhydian de Rondell took the Grand Tour's final glory. The nation's Challenger in Waiting was recast as a Dawnish Assembly appointment without a tourney.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: only through Spiral Castle, home of House de Casillon, whose Reeve promised to contribute to the fayre.
n.Urizen: A Urizen sentinel was one of the few to complete every stage of the Grand Tour, and was invited to compete in the final contest at Anvil.

t.Astolat: Torag Meliora, earl of House Meliora of Astolat, was the sitting Knight-protector of Autumn going into the tourney, and was considered a favourite if they re-entered.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen sentinel who completed the Grand Tour came from Morrow.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in Knightly Redoubt, one of the items the Silver Nightingales offered under a rejected proposal for the Challenger in Waiting.
t.Semmerholm: The Moon Weavers who dwell near the Semmerstones made the magical weapon for the Grand Tour champion. The election of Semmerholm's senator was held between the Autumn tourney and the final contests.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Reeve of House de Casillon, who hail from Spiral Castle, agreed to provide something for the fayre.

The first shot.d: Corey Wayfarer's mandate committed the Navarr to war. The war itself begins only once the trod network links all six remaining vallorn hearts, and the Sarangrave and Visokuma in Axos are still unconnected. More than two thirds of stridings plan to settle, doubling the Navarr army cap to six. That capacity will shrink if no new army is begun by the Spring Equinox 387YE. Each army costs 200 mithril and 75 thrones, with regional substitutions offered: artisan materials in Hercynia, weirwood in Therunin, and an eternal's aid in Miaren. Druj, Thule, Jotun and Axou lands are all threatened. By the end of the Autumn Equinox no armies had been mustered, and the Imperial Orc and Wintermark support mandates had lapsed.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named; it is covered only by the general warning that the vallorn will attack virtually every Imperial nation once the trods are joined.
n.Druj: The Druj hold the Sarangrave, whose vallorn heart must be linked to the trods. They are unlikely to cooperate and may tear the trods down, though they might be able to contain the heart.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Axos's lingering grudge over its failed alliance with the Grendel slavers is cited as a reason relations with the Axou remain poor.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly was offered a mandate asking the Ethengraw to set the Black Forge to equipping a Hercynian army, at the cost of their own forge hammers order. It was not raised and the opportunity has passed.
n.Jotun: The Liathaven vallorn heart is already connected to the trod network, and its eruption when the final war begins will be a huge problem for the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The nation has committed itself irrevocably to war on the vallorn. Most stridings are returning to settle, the army cap has doubled to six, and the nation now faces the costly task of raising new armies and completing the trod network with allies' help.
n.Thule: The vallorn heart in Sküld in Thule lands is already linked to the trods, so the coming war will threaten the Thule as much as the Empire.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the northern vallorn lies on the border between Otkodov and Varushka, and Varushkan opportunities to support the Navarr are covered in a separate wind of fortune.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly was offered a mandate asking the artisans of Runegrott to arm a new Hercynian army, at the cost of the Keeper's own forging. It was not raised and the opportunity has passed.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: members of stridings that become steadings may take a new resource in Brocéliande without the normal charge.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is named as a neighbour of Hercynia and home to some of the Empire's most skilled smiths.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia can now support a new Navarr army rich in artisans from the restored forges at Treji. If it is raised by the end of Summer Solstice 388YE, artisan materials may be substituted for mithril at 40 per wain.
t.Liathaven: The Liathaven vallorn heart is already connected to the trod network and will become a grave danger once the final war begins.
t.Miaren: Returning Navarr are gathering in Miaren, which can now support a new army full of vates. Through a plenipotentiary, that army could seek the aid of one of five interested eternals.
t.Otkodov: The vallorn on Otkodov's border with Varushka threatens the Thule. Otkodov is also where Navarr smiths from Treji were once taken in slavery.
t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave heart must be linked to the trods, which requires finding a Spring regio there. Only the Seventh Wave, the Narwhal's Spear or the Wolves of War could locate one, and the Druj may destroy any trods made.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a neighbour of Hercynia and home to some of the Empire's most skilled smiths.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is not named; it is attached only through the general warning that the vallorn will threaten nearly every Imperial nation.
t.Therunin: Therunin, where Druj invaders are being pushed back, can now support a new army of herbalists. With Great Forest Orc help it could substitute weirwood for mithril one-for-one if raised by the end of Summer Solstice 388YE.

r.Otkodov/Sküld: The vallorn heart in Sküld is already joined to the trod network, so it will awaken when the final war begins.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The Sarangrave heart lies in the warded ruined city of Béantal Dol, and a Spring regio must be found nearby to connect it to the trods.

The gathering storm.d: Four Wrecks captains (Murchadh Lughaidh, the Black Corsair, the Reaver of Attar and Friar Arwenack) planned an Autumn ceremony drawing on the Lictors to form a navy based at Atalaya. Each captain killed would reduce its starting strength by 1250, and three or more deaths would prevent it entirely. The Turn of the Gyre coven sought to cast an empowered Thunderous Deluge over Madruga, and stopping them would end the Wrecks' large Spring rituals for a year. Scouts also found the Storm's Child figurehead and a Grendel Sand Mage holding the Chest of Sand boon. Wrecker raids threatened the House of Guerra, a Kruidenkenner caravan in Necropolis, and Spiral.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named in an out-of-character note as a threat that cannot reproduce the Empire's options.
n.Grendel: The Grendel spymaster Sea-Wraith supplied the intelligence, though scouts found he had withheld details, and a Grendel Sand Mage, Arhrun Fhearghes, held the stolen Chest of Sand. A Wrecks navy would threaten Grendel coasts as well as the Empire's.
n.Highguard: Wreckers landed in Highguard's territory of Necropolis to hunt a Kruidenkenner caravan, putting the Kruidenkenner Trademaster's herb supply at risk.
n.The Brass Coast: The Wrecks gathered on the Freeborn Plain where the Freeborn nation was born, and the Storm's Child figurehead offered a chance to upgrade a Freeborn fleet or rally families to revive the Freeborn Storm navy. Wreckers also threatened pilgrims at the House of Guerra.
n.The League: The Wailing Gyre coven, funded by Azzura di Cazarri, planned to curse Spiral with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea, and its senator, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, was charged with stopping them.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: one of the four Wrecks captains, Friar Arwenack, sails with a cursed crew of Mitwold sailors.

t.Bay of Catazar: A Wrecks navy operating from Free Landing would be able to strike coastal territories right around the Bay, and Kruidenkenner herb trade across the Bay was threatened by wreckers.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies were noted as having pushed past the Grendel in Madruga to enter Feroz.
t.Madruga: Madruga was the battleground, where the Wrecks sought to found a navy and the Turn of the Gyre planned to unleash an empowered Thunderous Deluge, while wreckers raided the House of Guerra, whose Hand, Ahshen i Fiel i Guerra, had to defend the pilgrims or see the sinecure's output halved for a year.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Friar Arwenack's cursed crew aboard the Barrel of Best are described as Mitwold sailors.
t.Necropolis: Wreckers hunted a Kruidenkenner caravan nearing the magazijn, and if Trademaster Bernardo Von Temeschwar failed, the exchange would be limited to 24 cerulean mazzarine and 33 random herbs for two seasons.
t.Spiral: The Wailing Gyre planned to curse Spiral with a non-empowered Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea that would still cause widespread coastal destruction, even threatening Apulian.

r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Children of Wrecks massed on the Freeborn Plain outside Atalaya, where four captains planned to found a navy using the captured marina as home port, and where the Storm's Child figurehead and Chest of Sand could be recovered.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: A wrecker fleet landed in Longbeach and spent a week tracking the Kruidenkenner caravan towards the magazijn.

The tale that speaks to your heart.d: Following Maarit Suvidottir's mandate, Imperial fleets fighting Asavea in the Sea of Salt now receive rings, liao, metals and the Frieøyer healing brew 'Oilybrag'. Imperial traders visiting Zemeh also do better business. The Sevenfold Path and Rod and Shield each gain ten liao a season for two fortification rituals. Censor Oxtitocszin declined two Spring curses, showed interest in rituals that help or hinder spies, and denied any dealings with Yaw'nagrah. Gifts were promised for Rafe of Wintermark and for the rescuers of Präst Kauitalic. The Sumaah asked to see the evidence that Vardas was not real. They also welcomed Emperor Vesna's letter and said an emissary would deliver a gift to Ambassador Accalon.

n.Highguard: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was central to the exchanges, and an emissary from the High House of Pride is due at Anvil to present a gift to Accalon at the Highborn camp.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is one of only two nations whose ships did not sail west to aid Sumaah, because the mandate lacked a greater majority there.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is one of only two nations whose ships did not sail west to aid Sumaah, because the mandate lacked a greater majority there.
n.Wintermark: Rafe of Wintermark's mandate to support Sumaah was superseded by Maarit Suvidottir's, but the House of Pride is sending him twenty liao and four bottles of Frygtede øglebryg in thanks.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah would rather Asaveans look to Timoj than to Bastion for their understanding of the Way, though they judge spreading the faith more important.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah embassy is in Necropolis, and the civil service could send copies of the Saul and Vardas research there.

The wild wind rises.d: Some twenty-two thousand Imperial fighters and six thousand Summer heralds faced eleven Jotun armies. The Frozen Citadel in Southmoor fell first. Farstrider's Watch held for four days before its gates fell, and the Singing Caves were lost, though the miners escaped with a final mithril shipment. King Gudmunder Arasonn rebuked Stephen of Sarcombe and placed Honour's Rest under his protection, and he again recognised Jarl Haakon as Jarl of the Mourn. Freemoor, Alderly and Green March remain free, and miners wage a guerrilla war in the Ore Hills. The Mournwold loses its Senator. General Stanley of Chalkdown must stand or break his oath, with a chance to rescue the miners' leaders at Jade Wood.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly's mandate saw the vigilant unconquered clear most of Jarl Haakon's caches in Southmoor. Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum is charged with raiding the last and best-defended cache.
n.Jotun: Eleven Jotun armies under King Gudmunder Arasonn and Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir conquered half the Mournwold, and Jarl Haakon was again recognised as Jarl of the Mourn. The king's protection of Honour's Rest opened a rift with Stephen of Sarcombe and his yegarra.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step left a safe Miaren to fight in the Mournwold, but captured Navarr were denied the Choice and honourable burial, and were beheaded and left for carrion.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun king praised the Brass Coast's honour in letting the mound at Fort Braydon be raised, and two Jotun armies arrived fresh from a failed strike into northern Kahraman.
n.The League: Jarl Helgarn's warband raided Tassato Mestra for ilium from the Tassatan Hills, and Custodian Serafina di Sarvos is responsible for stopping it. Workers at the Orchard of the Watch are to be escorted back to Tassato.
n.The Marches: The Tusks and the Mournwold's yeomen, beaters, miners and Marcher orcs fought hard but lost four regions and their Senator. General Stanley of Chalkdown now faces breaking his oath, a fate that once sent Nedry of the Cullachs into the Wicker Man.
n.Wintermark: The Green Shield fought at the forefront alongside the Shadowed Flame and faerie knights. The Bloodcloaks recovered and tended the fallen, but both armies were forced back with the rest of the Imperial host.

t.Bregasland: The Southern Bear left the Burhfæst in Bregasland to join the Mournwold assault. A Jotun warband is hunting Moon-That-Sings Feni in the Grey Fens.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the Tusks' recent fighting against the Lasambrian orcs and to the Lasambrian Jotun resting after their defeat in the Cinnabar Hills.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Helgarn, who led the ilium raid into Tassato, is of Vallorberg.
t.Kahraman: The Tusks marched north through Braydon's Jasse to reach the Mournwold. The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder came to the Mourn straight from their failed strike into northern Kahraman.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven was the staging ground from which eleven Jotun armies poured into the Mournwold. If the Feni are saved, Liath's Ring could come under threat from the Empire.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: with Cold Sun destroyed, Miaren was safe for the moment, freeing the Quiet Step to march to the Mournwold.
t.Mitwold: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield marched south after their furlough in Mitwold. The Black Canal now gives Mitwold only reduced benefits while Chalkdowns and Southmoor are in Jotun hands.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun took four of its regions, so the Mournwold is no longer Imperial, has no Senator and cannot be targeted from the Anvil regio. Its people now face the Choice and punishing tithes.
t.Tassato: Jarl Helgarn's warband struck into Tassato Mestra to steal ilium. Imperial labourers from the Orchard of the Watch are to be escorted back to Tassato under Jotun guarantee.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: fast-moving light infantry from Tromsa strengthened Queen Yrsa's vanguard.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shield and Bloodcloaks set out after their furlough there, the Green Shield 'from fine Upwold feasting'.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A Jotun warband is pursuing the Moon-That-Sings Feni here, and the Imperial Advisor for the Feni, Syn Truth-Walker Returned, is responsible for stopping it.
r.Hordalant/Vallorberg: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Helgarn, leader of the warband raiding the Tassatan Hills, is of Vallorberg.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks marched north through Braydon's Jasse into the Greensward.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: If the Empire saves the Moon-That-Sings Feni, they offer to help the next Imperial army attack Liath's Ring from Bregasland, which would put the region under threat.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun spared Liaven's Glen, and the Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder moved through it into the Mourn.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Alderly remained free of the Jotun at the season's end, at least for the moment.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The last battle, at Lindenford farm, ended in Jotun conquest of the Chalkdowns. The Happiston titles lost their production, and the Black Canal's benefits were cut until the region is reclaimed.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Freemoor remains in Imperial hands, and the Tusks fell back there to the sanctuary of Landskeeper's Bulwark.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March remains free, but it is under threat from the traitor Dalton Royse's network. Nigel Hornbeam must kill him at Charlie's Coppice to lift that threat.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Farstrider's Watch fell after four days and Jarl Haakon is reportedly setting up his hall there. King Arasonn placed Honour's Rest and the Orchard of the Watch under his protection.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Jotun overran the Ore Hills and the Singing Caves, but miners fight on as guerrillas. Their encircled leaders at Jade Wood could be rescued and won over to the Tusks.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The Frozen Citadel was overwhelmed and Southmoor fell to the Jotun. The Highborn's cache-clearing has lifted the threat there, leaving one last cache to raid.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Jarl Helgarn's warband struck into the northern hills to steal ilium for the Jarl of Mists. Custodian Serafina di Sarvos must stop him or lose the Hills' ilium at the Winter Solstice.

Thresher's summer.d: Inspired by Clytemnestra of the House of the Wanderer, Urizeni visitors spread across Upwold and Mitwold. Some reached Bregasland, and those who went to Mournwold retreated before the Jotun invasion. Their willingness to endure gruelling work such as threshing won grudging respect, and every farm became a little more profitable. Jedediah Boon's Marcher friars found their beliefs about reincarnation as trees dismissed, but shriving and their pastoral guidance fascinated Urizeni priests. Urizen congregations swelled while Marcher spiritual matters were neglected. The architect Tacitus proposed a Landskeeper's Study at Oakwood where Urizen mana could be sold, and the empty Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro could become a monastery for debate. The Senate approved both, and they will benefit from each other while both endure.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having sacked the Temple of the Four Winds before it was completed, until they were driven out of Morrow.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun invasion of the Mournwold forced Urizeni visitors there to retreat.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms received hundreds of Urizeni helpers for the harvest, making each a little more profitable and building respect between the nations. Marcher friars sent east earned admiration in Urizen, although spiritual matters at home were neglected in their absence.
n.Urizen: Urizeni mages, sentinels and scholars learned first-hand how hard farm work is and won Marcher respect. Visiting friars swelled Urizen congregations, raising their liao and votes, and sparked intense interest in shriving.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: a few Urizeni visitors travelled as far as Bregasland to help with the harvest.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was one of the two main territories where Urizeni visitors spread out to help farmers bring in the harvest.
t.Morrow: Marcher monks were housed at the empty Temple of the Four Winds in Morrow, which became a thriving centre of debate. The Senate chose to convert it into a permanent monastery.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni visitors went to the Mournwold but were forced to retreat in the face of the Jotun invasion.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the architect Tacitus, who proposed the Landskeeper's Study, came from the Spire of the White Sun in Redoubt.
t.Upwold: Upwold was a main destination for the Urizeni harvest helpers, and the Senate chose to build the Landskeeper's Study there to share farm magic and sell Urizen mana.

r.Morrow/Peregro: The Temple of the Four Winds in Peregro hosted Marcher monks and Urizeni priests, and the Senate chose to repurpose it as the Monastery of the Four Winds with a new Urizeni arbiter, liao and garden income.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Tacitus stayed with the short-handed monks of Oakwood in Ashbrook, where the Senate chose to build the Landskeeper's Study for visiting Urizen architects to discuss farm magic and sell mana.

Tourney of the Damned.d: After two champions, one Dawnish and one Varushkan, defeated the knight a year earlier, his bargain went awry and his rampage began. Heroes limited his strength to a standard army, but it raises those it kills, and would gain about 1000 effective strength each season it went unchallenged. The two original champions could force him to a grand melee if they found him, likely in Wickmoor or Skoremujac, via an as-yet-unfound Sentinel Gate conjunction. Research commissioned by Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti might help. Executing him would leave his unliving troops rampaging, needing an army in each territory to contain them at up to 500 casualties; permanently destroying him would make them fall lifeless.

n.Dawn: Dawn faced an army of the dead that sought to conquer it as a kingdom of the dead, and one of the two original champions plus Dawnish warriors were needed for the challenging warband.
n.Varushka: A creature of the Varushkan Howling Queen threatened Karov, and the Varushkan champion and Varushkan warriors were required to challenge it, while Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti's commissioned research might reveal the knight's location.

t.Karov: Karov was the other possible target of the army of the dead, and would need a defending army to contain rampaging unliving soldiers even if the knight were killed.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was one of the two possible targets of the knight's army after the Autumn Equinox, facing massive loss of life and possible permanent scarring if no army defended it.

r.Karov/Skoremujac: Skoremujac was one of the two likely places where the knight was gathering his forces and where the challenge might be issued, if the precise location could be found.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: Wickmoor was one of the two likely places where the knight was gathering his forces and where the champions might confront him in a grand melee.

True faith.d: Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower released the Library's findings, backed by statements in the Vigilance, Wisdom and Varushkan Assemblies, and confidence in the Synod faltered. Three paths were offered: a mandate declaring that it does not matter whether paragons are real, a greater-majority judgement of recognition removing Vardas, or a mandate denouncing the findings as lies, which would destroy the Library. Masha Sigeling called Hazelelponi to inquisition. While the crisis lasted, new inspirational memorials had no effect, the Capodomus Cathedral consecration guidance was delayed, and no new mandates could support the Grand Inspiration. The General Assembly revoked Vardas' recognition and defeated The Fool of Glory's stories-over-facts mandate.

n.Dawn: Dawn's existing mandate urging its people to support the Grand Inspiration of the Way still resolved normally, with its contribution due to be completed shortly before the Winter Solstice.
n.Highguard: Highguard's call to support the sacred city of the Grand Inspiration continued, but the crisis blocked any new mandates in its support. The faithful also questioned the pilgrimage to Bastion as a sign of the paragon.
n.Navarr: Navarr was unable to restate its support for the Grand Inspiration of the Way while the crisis of faith lasted.
n.The League: The evidence held that a League mountebank penned the stories of Vardas. The League's Grand Inspiration contribution still resolved normally, but guidance on consecrating Capodomus Cathedral was delayed.
n.Urizen: Urizen, troubled by its own recent experience with an inspirational figure, would have been left in disastrous crisis had a reassurance mandate passed without a greater majority.
n.Varushka: Vardas was a much-loved figure in Varushka, and the Varushkan Assembly urged the faithful to look instead to the real deeds of Varushkan wardens once attributed to the fictional paragon.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was unable to restate its support for the Grand Inspiration of the Way while the crisis of faith lasted.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the pilgrimage to Bastion, one of the signs of a paragon, was questioned because many older paragons appear to predate Bastion itself.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa marshes were cited as a sacred site the Synod could still consecrate whatever the outcome.
t.Sarvos: The writ to consecrate Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos was upheld, but its guidance and supporting mandate were delayed until the crisis of faith was resolved. Aldones di Sarvos's past life vision was also cited as an earlier case that led to a paragon being de-recognised.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Houndsgate in the Barrens was cited as a sacred site the Synod could still consecrate.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa marshes were named as an example of a sacred site that could still be consecrated.

Unspoken words.d: With winter approaching and their numbers more than tripled, the Rahvin agreed to send their negotiator Jannik to Anvil after invitations from the Imperial Orcs and the Dawnish Assembly. Jannik was willing to meet Claude Deeds on neutral ground. The Dawnish Assembly rejected settling the Barrens but called for Dawn to defend its foreigners, and it was suggested that Dawnish generals might bind their armies by oath to protect the Rahvin and Great Forest Orcs. Meanwhile the Lone Path Striding and the Karass scout Canta came to Anvil to warn of new trods and Druj magic in the Untrod Groves. Following talks with the Karass, the senator permitted knights to explore the Groves.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Assembly rejected settling the Barrens but called for its foreigners to be defended, its generals were challenged to swear a binding oath protecting the Rahvin and Great Forest Orcs, and its knights won the chance to explore the Untrod Groves for riches.
n.Druj: A Karass scout detected Druj magic enchanting a new path through the Untrod Groves, while many of the Black Wind had fled into Druj lands and the Rahvin continued to seek escape from the Druj yoke.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest of Peytaht is described as stretching from Broken Ride in Highguard-held Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly invited the Rahvin back to Anvil to find a way for them to survive winter, and Jannik declared himself eager to talk with his friends among the Imperial Orcs.
n.Navarr: The Lone Path Striding, travelling through the Untrod Groves on new trods, lost Emyri Lonepath for a day and came to Anvil with the Karass scout Canta to speak with the Barrens senator and interested Navarr; the Navarr oath to defend the Great Forest Orcs was held up as an example.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkans are noted as having slaughtered the last of the Montanians in Hope's Rest, and Ossium is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the far north of Sermersuaq is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Lone Path Striding intended to return to Miaren, where their journey began, anticipating the end of the fight against the vallorn.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: its far corners are named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest of Peytaht is said to stretch from Broken Ride in Reikos across the southern Barrens.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: its far north is named among the remote places the Lone Path Striding walk.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens remained unsettled and uneasy as the Rahvin faced winter at the Fangs, Dawn debated defending its foreign peoples, and new trods and Druj magic were discovered in the Untrod Groves, which Dawnish knights went on to explore.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: referenced only in further reading about an earlier invasion of Therunin.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: named in Viviane Knotes' judgement as a Dawnish territory whose loss would be no more acceptable than that of the Barrens.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: Mentioned in passing: identified as the starting point of the Great Forest of Peytaht that stretches across the southern Barrens.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Mentioned in passing: the remaining Black Wind who did not flee are noted as confined to the Bitter Strand, where the vetoed Rahvin treaty would have granted land.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat are said to be desperate to claim Farweald, which is listed among regions Dawn could settle without displacing anyone.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Mentioned in passing: noted as home of the Great Forest Orcs whom the Navarr have sworn to treat as family.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Mentioned in passing: noted as emptied after Varushka slaughtered the last Montanians, leaving only the ruins of Dourfell Keep, and as the hills where the Untrod Groves begin.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Mentioned in passing: the Untrod Groves are said to stretch to the very edge of the Plain of Teeth.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: New trods tainted with Druj magic were found running through the Groves, a Navarr strider went missing there, and after the senator's negotiations with the Karass, Dawnish knights were able to explore the region for iridescent gloaming, beggarwood and dragonbone.

Upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs.d: The motion cost 80 weirwood and 30 thrones (240 crowns), with six months to complete. Chiara Zayden Riqueza supplied 29 thrones 7 crowns and the 80 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE, and Rhys Nighthaven gave the final crown. The Red Wind Corsairs gained the Forayers quality. When defending a coastal region of the Bay of Catazar they can use the Take to the Sea or Take to the Land order, spending a vulnerable season becoming a navy or reverting to an army. When attacking they can use the Daring Raid order, reflecting their instinct to take defeated enemies' money rather than their lives.

n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that some Wintermark armies dislike fighting alongside a foraying army, though many Wintermark heroes prefer ransoming defeated enemies to butchering them and have no reason to dislike a daring army.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay of Catazar is currently the only place the Red Wind Corsairs can use their new ability. While defending a coastal region there, they can take to the sea as a navy or return to land.

Victory and unity.d: Ilarch Maxatios said Axos could not lead opposition to the Freedom Accord. He also declined to explain a white granite purchase and refused Imperial scholars access to study the sorcerer-kings. Rumours spoke of outside funding for Issyk's docks and of Jarmish-backed construction at Maykop, which might anger the Commonwealth. Kyther, aided by Theodosia of Ipotavo's liao-fuelled preaching, urged the citadels to unite. The Regario Dossier, a Conclave order or the Synod might act on several opportunities, including joining the exorcism of Solokha. Sophia Anacharsis did visit Anvil, and several cardinals received items hallowed with auras of understanding, which proved controversial. The Shuttered Lantern was sent to investigate Kyther and Theodosia.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: an Axou preacher warned the Druj might strike again across the Path of the Eye, though Kyther's talk of threatening military powers was not aimed solely at them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel once partly destroyed Issyk's expanded docks in retaliation when Axos joined the Liberty Pact and ended their short-lived alliance.
n.Navarr: Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr, the Ambassador to Axos, led Imperial diplomacy with Ilarch Maxatios. Fintan pressed the Axou on the Freedom Accord, granite, the sorcerer-kings and memory magic, and was expected to escort Sophia Anacharsis to the Assembly of Nine.
n.Urizen: The Axou blame Urizeni emissaries for the fall of Solokha, and Imperial historical testimony partly corroborates this. Any Urizen role in Synod statements on the Solokha exorcism would therefore be particularly sensitive.

t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the Tsark debacle in the Mountains of the Moon is cited as the source of Axou bitterness towards the Empire, and some Axou mourners lost kin there.

We all stand.d: The serendipity enchantment helped Imperials meet locals, but it also helped those hostile to the Imperial Orcs find each other. The Golden Pyramid kept exploring, gaining resources each season. Talks over Beoraidh's docks stalled on steep tariffs. The Conclave disseminated Gift of the Wily Broker to the Black Sand Circle in exchange for Eye of Ruby and Sapphire. Proposals were raised for a cerulean mazzarine garden in Nadir, Tamazi fortifications in Eoradal and Fleisardh, and a Greater Apulian Way through Spiral. Both the Marcher and Freeborn assemblies sent farmers to help with Mareave's arid land. The Senate made the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons an Imperial Orc position. The Master of Rings commissioned Curstag's Way, linking Redoubt, Spiral and Mareave.

n.Grendel: The Tamazi pitched their proposed forts as protection against Grendel attack, while Golden Pyramid magicians made contact with former Grendel wizards of the Black Sand Circle in Beoraidh.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn members of the Golden Pyramid were among those seeking access to Beoraidh's docks.
n.Imperial Orcs: Tamazi orcs proposed fortifications and a Skouran embassy, and a Yerende orc proposed a cerulean mazzarine sinecure. The nation gained Marcher and Freeborn farming aid and was awarded the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons as a national position.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that farmers in Bregasland felt they had nothing to offer Mareave's arid grasslands.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the proposed roadside rest stops in Spiral were to be patterned after Navarr wayhouses.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly agreed to urge farmers, including Zemress islanders, to help make Mareave flower. This cost every Brass Coast congregation a rank of production, and the farmers expect recompense.
n.The League: Bishop Fabio's call for trade through Spiral inspired Leaguers to propose the Greater Apulian Way. The Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, commissioned Curstag's Way to connect Redoubt, Spiral and Mareave.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly agreed to send farmers to Mareave, drawing pious farmers away from Mitwold and Upwold. The farmers expect to be repaid for their efforts.
n.Urizen: Nightshadow spire architects co-devised the Greater Apulian Way and offered mithril if the Urizen assembly backed it. Urizen architects of the Golden Pyramid explored trade in Beoraidh.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a likely market for Mareave's cerulean mazzarine.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as a likely market for Mareave's cerulean mazzarine.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the League's work on the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion is cited as why few Leaguers initially took up Fabio's call.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn farmers would travel to the far side of the Bay of Catazar to reach Mareave.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland's farmers are noted as believing they have nothing to offer arid Mareave.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is cited as needing rebuilding, a reason some felt farmers should look closer to home.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the engineer Lucia Calumo di Apulian originally hails from Holberg.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is cited as needing rebuilding, a reason some felt farmers should look closer to home.
t.Mareave: Mareave lay under a serendipity enchantment that aided friends and foes alike. It became the focus of Golden Pyramid exploration, fortification and herb-garden proposals, Marcher and Freeborn farming aid, and a new trade road linking it to the Empire.
t.Mitwold: With Marcher farmers sent to Mareave, every congregation in Mitwold suffers a one-rank penalty for the season.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is invaded, and its farmers have more pressing matters than Mareave.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Mazzar Tulk had lived her life in Ossium and Skarsind before travelling to Mareave.
t.Redoubt: Curstag's Way, commissioned by the Master of Rings, will connect Redoubt with Spiral and Mareave, reviving the old road route from Apulian to Redoubt.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a natural market for cerulean mazzarine and as one of Mazzar Tulk's former homes.
t.Spiral: Spiral was the site of the proposed Greater Apulian Way, with mithril-infused roadhouses to ease travel despite the Black Plateau. The Master of Rings commissioned Curstag's Way through the territory.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.
t.Upwold: With Marcher farmers sent to Mareave, every congregation in Upwold suffers a one-rank penalty for the season.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Golden Pyramid trade talks for Beoraidh's docks stalled over steep tariffs. The Black Sand Circle at Execution Hill traded Eye of Ruby and Sapphire for Gift of the Wily Broker.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Tamazi proposed converting Rucraic's Redoubt into the Storm Lords Sentinel, a fortification ready to serve as a Skouran embassy. They also eyed rebuilding a ruined aqueduct to bring fresh water.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Tamazi proposed High Mountain Home, a storm-warded mountain fortress meant to awe the Brine Turtles, but the opportunity has since expired.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion's under-developed state raised building costs across Mareave. The Greater Apulian Way proposal would have removed that quality and placed an inn and warehouses near the old lighthouse ruins.
r.Mareave/Nadir: The Lazuline Bowl in central Nadir offers ideal conditions for cerulean mazzarine, and a sinecure creating a Lazuline Bonetender was proposed. It is illegal while the local orcs are still considered barbarians.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus is the proposed site of the Greater Apulian Way great work, which would raise investment for Spiral's businesses.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the Black Plateau horror squatting in the centre of Screed is cited as the reason travel through Spiral is so hard.

Where five winds meet.d: Asavean warships that raided Meade had gathered in Faraden waters, where Asavean agents court anti-Imperial nobles. The Celestial Arch was sent to investigate the Asavean threat. Faraden merchants refused to pay the Ambassador's wain prices. The Tchemetzi family offered 75 Thrones or a Spring ritual text for 25 wains of weirwood. The Blue Silken Scarf sought gloaming through the City of Gold and Lead. Faraden musicians now visit the Azure Chorus, and an architect proposed a parador there. Mistress Karadragha floated a Faraden enclave in Holberg, offered a delegation to Anvil (matched by one to Asavea), and the Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans are noted to have intervened militarily to aid the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan might trade with along the Blood Red Roads.
n.Jotun: Jotun lands separate the Empire from Faraden, and Jotun tariffs weigh on overland caravans. The Lasambrian Jotun invasion of Kahraman is noted as having ended in defeat for the orcs.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Owain Farkas of Navarr was briefly the last Overseer of the Gloaming Road before the title was abrogated and his bid returned.
n.The Brass Coast: Faraden performers now visit the Azure Chorus, earning the Azure Sutannir Mina i Yashum i Riqueza an extra 2 crowns a season. Erdene Bataguin asked the Freeborn assembly to welcome Faraden pilgrims and offered to design a parador there if it does.
n.The League: Mistress Karadragha asked whether the League would accept a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg. She suggested their priests might be consulted, and said it would make an Imperial enclave in Caitun easier to offer in return.
n.The Marches: The Asavean raid on Meade, launched from Faraden waters, is at the centre of the diplomatic dilemma facing the Marcher Ambassador Ebenezer. The Tchemetzi politely declined his offer to send Marcher landskeepers to Pelabuhan.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan might trade with on the way to Holberg.

t.Holberg: Faraden expressed interest in establishing a trading enclave in the city of Holberg, pending the League's willingness.
t.Kahraman: With the Lasambrian Jotun invasion defeated, work was completed on securing Kahraman's roads, a project that used Faraden kamkrags and builders of the Bataguin family.
t.Mitwold: The Asavean surprise attack on Meade was repulsed, with one warship sunk and another damaged. Its origin in Faraden waters prompted the diplomatic questions on this page.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Faraden superstition about the dangers of the Sea of Snows, including cambion whales, explains their wariness of trading by sea.
t.Segura: The Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road, ending the overland trade of Faraden mithril for gloaming through Segura.

Where the river rises.d: The flood killed perhaps two hundred people, injured twice as many and left many homeless, sick and hungry. Lord Rain's heralds lamented that his offer to spare all lives had been refused. The Cerevado Nets were wrecked, though the seat holder received eight rings of ilium this season, and every bridge except the Sobral Bridge was destroyed. This cut the Sunset Roads and stopped armies crossing between Madruga and Segura or Feroz. Madruga now has seven regions, and no one holds a usable map for scrying it. Fausta Ankarien guided the Silver Chalice to give aid, and the Conclave sent the Rod and Shield and the Unfettered Mind to explore the marshes. The Cerevado Nets remain unrepaired.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish difficulties in the Barrens are cited as a sign of the challenges the Freeborn will face in reclaiming Feroz.
n.Grendel: The Grendel forces in northern Siroc Plains were caught off guard by the floodwaters, which scattered their scouts and baggage trains from the siege of Oran. They still notionally hold the new marsh there, and their commander at Mora's Rock in Feroz shows no sign of surrendering.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the challenges the Imperial Orcs face in Mareave are given as an example of what awaits the Freeborn in Feroz.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Sobral Bridge survived partly because it was reinforced for Imperial armies during the Lasambrian Jotun occupation of Segura, and Bregasland's marshes are used as a comparison.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a liberated Therunin going to the Navarr is cited as an example of how certain it is that Feroz will be assigned to the Brass Coast.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn bore the cost of their own ritual: hundreds were killed, injured or displaced along the Scorrero, the Sunset Roads were severed and the Cerevado Nets were ruined. They must also decide whether to reclaim a Feroz left wrecked by Rahab, which is expected to be assigned to them.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's marshes are named as a comparison for the new marsh in Madruga.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan experience in Ossium is cited as a sign of the challenges of reclaiming Feroz.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's assignment to Wintermark is used as a comparison for Feroz, and Kallavesa's marshes are compared with the new Madrugan marsh.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the swollen river between Lightsea and Siroc Plains now flows more swiftly than ever into the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Bregasland.
t.Feroz: Feroz largely escaped the flood, but losing the bridge between Oranseri and Siroc Plains cut it off from Madruga. Wrecked by Rahab and abandoned by the Freeborn, it will need major investment to rebuild, and Grendel and Children of Wrecks forces still hold regions there.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Holberg.
t.Kahraman: The flooding began in Kahraman's mountains, and many riverside settlements were washed away before their priests received the warning. The Silver Chalice could offer aid here, and the Sobral Bridge still links the territory to Segura.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the new Madrugan marsh is likened to the marshes of Kallavesa.
t.Madruga: The Blight was washed away, but the southern Great Grasses and Siroc Plains became a steaming, magic-infused marsh, and the ruins of Siroc were swept away or sunk. The territory now has seven regions, cannot be scried with any existing map, and remains outside Imperial control.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs' challenges in Mareave are cited as a comparison for rebuilding Feroz.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the challenges the Varushkans faced in Ossium are cited as a comparison for rebuilding Feroz.
t.Segura: Segura took the brunt of the flood: the Cerevado waterfront was flattened, the Cerevado Nets were ruined and the Cerevado Bridge was lost, cutting the Sunset Roads off from the wider Empire. Only the Sobral Bridge still stands.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's assignment to Wintermark is used as a comparison for the expected assignment of Feroz.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish challenges in the Barrens are cited as a comparison for reclaiming Feroz.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: a liberated Therunin going to the Navarr is used as a comparison for Feroz's expected assignment.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse is back under Imperial control and still gives easy access to Segura despite the flood's disruption.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: Spring magics worked by the Children of Wrecks here and in Free Landing may have made the sea rise to meet the flood.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Rivermouth Bridge linking Oranseri to Siroc Plains was destroyed, so armies can no longer cross between Feroz and Madruga.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The floodwaters thundered through arid Gambit, flooding riverside villages and wrecking farms and their irrigation ditches.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Floodwater ran down the hills, briefly making it hard for workers to reach the Damatian Cliffs, which were otherwise undisrupted. Rumours of Inacia's Trove drew treasure hunters to the riverbanks, but nothing was found.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound remains under Imperial dominance, and the waters receded away from it to leave fertile, if strangely altered, grasslands nearby.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing stays under the Children of Wrecks, whose Spring magics there may have helped the sea rise to meet the flood.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The river on Lightsea's border with Siroc Plains burst its banks. The old Siroc Bridge still stands, but the shifting banks may yet wash it away.
r.Madruga/Torres: Torres remains under Imperial dominance, and the receding waters left fertile plains of unusual grasses and odd beasts to its south.
r.Segura/Burnish: The flood surged through Burnish, washing out riverside villages, ruining buildings and destroying farms and irrigation.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Cerevado's waterfront was flattened and people died, the Cerevado Nets were left in tatters and the Cerevado Bridge was swept away, severing the Sunset Roads.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: Sobral was badly hit, with its people given only enough warning to flee, but the reinforced Sobral Bridge survived as the only remaining crossing of the Scorrero.

You could be happy.d: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer (General Assembly) and Tuuli (Wisdom Assembly) passed judgements calling citizens to act against the Druj threat to the eastern territories. Any national assembly bordering the Druj could enact a mandate encouraging citizens to walk the border. This raises the victory points the Druj need to claim a beachhead to 25, at a cost of five thrones in taxation from each protected territory. All four eligible assemblies enacted it. Separately, Amris Johan Merikovich's judgement urged the Iron Helms to abandon cruelty for dark magics and curses. The resulting mandate was discussed, but Anastasiya Lukashovna Volkov had the Eyes of Loyalty turned on it.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly enacted the border mandate, so Dawnish citizens patrol the Barrens against Druj incursion at a cost of five thrones in taxation.
n.Druj: Citizen patrols along the borders of Dawn, Navarr, Urizen and Varushka mean the Druj now need 25 victory points to claim a beachhead in those territories. The patrols do not harm their armies or affect regions they claim after a beachhead.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is listed among the territories the Druj have claimed over the last ten years.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly enacted the border mandate, which protects Therunin once it is reclaimed and if it is assigned to Navarr, at a cost of five thrones in taxation.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the territories the Druj have claimed over the last ten years.
n.Thule: Varushka's border mandate does not extend to the Thule-held region of Webwood in Ossium, which remains without the citizen patrols.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly enacted the border mandate, setting citizens to patrol both Morrow and Zenith at a combined cost of ten thrones in taxation.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly enacted the border mandate protecting Ossium. It also considered a mandate to turn the Iron Helms from cruelty to dark magics and curses, but the Eyes of Loyalty were turned on that mandate.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Druj have laid claim to over the past decade.
t.Morrow: Urizeni citizens now patrol Morrow's border with the Druj, making a beachhead harder to claim, though the territory's taxation falls by five thrones.
t.Ossium: Still scarred by Druj devastation, Ossium is now patrolled by Varushkan citizens under their assembly's mandate. The Thule-held Webwood is not covered.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories the Druj have laid claim to over the past decade.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish citizens now patrol the Barrens, where the Druj remain active, at a cost of five thrones in taxation. The territory was also where the Iron Helms executed the leaders of the Black Wind.
t.Therunin: With the Druj still active in Therunin, Navarr's mandate will see citizens patrol its border once it is reclaimed, if it is assigned to Navarr.
t.Zenith: Under the Urizen mandate, citizens patrol Zenith's border with the Druj, making a beachhead harder to claim, at a cost of five thrones in taxation.

r.Ossium/Webwood: Because Webwood is held by Thule, the Varushkan border mandate does not extend to it, so it gains no protection from the citizen patrols.
